en.Q131162565: Alanya Lighthouse is a lighthouse in the Alanya district of Antalya.
en.Q131351734: Hisar Mosque is a mosque in the Hisar quarter of Didim, converted from a church.
en.Q131384363: Tabaklar Bath, also called Debbağlar Bath, is a stone double bathhouse in Bolu, on İzzet Baysal Street in the Tabaklar quarter, between Özek and Akbaba streets.
en.Q131390740: The Tomb of Cem Sultan is one of many tombs at the Muradiye Mosque complex, led by that of Sultan Murad II. Most of these tombs are of high artistic value, and the one called the Tomb of Cem Sultan is among the most elegant for its interior decoration.
en.Q131390755: This tomb belongs to Ahmed Bican Efendi, younger brother of Yazıcızade Mehmed Efendi, who was born in Gelibolu. A student of Hacı Bayram Veli, he taught with his brother at the madrasa in Gelibolu and translated his brother's Arabic work Megaribu'z-Zaman into Turkish as Envârü'l-Âşıkîn.
en.Q131390865: The Liman Baba Tomb and open-air prayer place are at the fishing harbour of İğneada, Demirköy (Kırklareli). Built in the Republican era, the site has three concrete structures: the tomb, an ablution fountain and a prayer platform. The turbaned gravestone inside is dated 1795, and the inscription outside 1856.
en.Q131390882: The Tomb of Nasreddin Hodja is the building that holds the grave of Nasreddin Hodja.
en.Q131390980: The Tomb of Merkez Efendi is in the garden of Merkez Efendi Mosque, in the Merkezefendi quarter of Topkapı, Zeytinburnu (Istanbul). It is run by the Istanbul Directorate of Tombs and is open to visitors.
en.Q131391518: The Tomb of Hallaj-i Mansur is a symbolic (maqam) tomb built in 1407 by İskender Bey, son of Hacı Pasha. It stands at the fork where the slope down to Hamzakoy beach meets the road to the Fener Tepesi area.
en.Q131391519: This tomb belongs to the scholar Yazıcıoğlu Mehmed. He was taught by his father Yazıcı Salih, learned Arabic and Persian, studied in Egypt and travelled through many Islamic lands; he was able to write works in Arabic and Persian.
en.Q131391812: This tomb belongs to Şerbetçi Baba, a dervish who fought beside Gazi Süleyman Pasha in the conquest of Gelibolu. He is counted among the Horasan dervishes known as the 'Abdalan-ı Rum'.
en.Q131402661: Zağnos (Zağanos) Bridge is a single round-arched bridge over the Kuzgun stream in Ortahisar, Trabzon, linking the Zindan and İmaret gates. It is named after Zağanos Pasha, who rebuilt it in 1467. Renewed and widened in 1888, it is thought once to have been a wooden drawbridge.
en.Q131402688: Tunca Bridge 2 is an arch bridge built under a large rock in the town of Tunca, 22 km from Ardeşen, Rize. It crosses the confluence of the Tunca and Selamet streams and is 20 metres long, 2.2 metres wide and 8 metres high. It once linked Tunca with the Durak valley.
en.Q131403316: Servetiye Bridge is a stone bridge in the Servetiye Karşı quarter of Başiskele, Kocaeli. Its building technique and materials resemble the stone bridges of the eastern Black Sea.
en.Q131403334: Golaşa Bridge, also called Golaşa Hanları or Taşgeçit Bridge, is a historic arch bridge over the Karadere in the village of Taşgeçit, Araklı (Trabzon). It was restored in 2019.
en.Q131406380: The Tomb of Bedreddin Pars Bey stands south of Şehreküstü Mosque in Bursa. It belongs to Bedreddin Mahmut Bey, known as "Pars Bey" in the reign of Murad I, and his son Yakup Bey.
en.Q131437249: Kurşunlu Han is a historic inn in the Şehzadeler district of Manisa, built in 1488 by Hüsnüşah Hatun, wife of Bayezid II, as part of the Hatuniye Mosque complex.
en.Q131523702: The Monastery of St Nicholas is a monastery in Mustafapaşa, Ürgüp.
en.Q131526556: Mar Petyun Chaldean Church is a historic Chaldean Catholic church in the Sur district of Diyarbakır, built in the 17th century.
en.Q131527192: This monastery in Mardin, belonging to the Syriac Orthodox Church, contains the Church of Mor Mihail. It was built in the 4th century and takes its name from Mor Mihayel, an important figure of the time.
en.Q131535497: The Dr. Ceyhun İrgil Health Museum of Nilüfer Municipality opened in 2024 in the İhsaniye quarter of Bursa. It displays medical objects and documents donated by Dr. Ceyhun İrgil and by health workers who lived and worked in Bursa and their families.
en.Q131555490: Kale Bath is a historic Turkish bath with men's and women's sections in the Vize district of Kırklareli. It is now derelict and out of use.
en.Q131681329: Ahlat Museum is an archaeology and city museum in Ahlat.
en.Q131738634: Lala Hüseyin Pasha Bath is a hamam in Kütahya.
en.Q131738681: Çoban Mustafa Pasha Bath is a hamam in Gebze. It belongs to the complex built by Çoban Mustafa Pasha, completed between 1522 and 1524. It is a symmetrical double bath in classical Ottoman style, built of rubble stone and brick.
en.Q131739131: Kemer Bath is a hamam in Kütahya.
en.Q131739220: Bekir Bey Bath is a bathhouse in Besni. Today it is in ruins and no longer used.
en.Q131741395: Güzelşeyh Pavilion (Güzel Şeyh Kasrı) is a pavilion in Altınakar, Diyarbakır.
en.Q131741415: Ak Medrese is a historic madrasa in central Niğde built in the Karamanid period. It is called the 'White Madrasa' for the whiteness of its stone and its richly carved marble portal, and is now a museum.
en.Q131744262: The Atatürk Memorial Museum is in the Şahinbey district of Gaziantep. To keep Atatürk's memory alive, the metropolitan municipality restored a historic house in the quarter where he was registered as a resident and opened the museum in 2013.
en.Q131744435: Erzincan Museum was founded in 1986 to display archaeological and ethnographic finds from the region.
en.Q131823656: La Fontaine Mansion is a Levantine mansion in Bornova, İzmir, opposite the Anglican Church of St Mary Magdalene and next to Murat Mansion. It now houses Ege University's Centre and Museum for Atatürk's Principles and the History of the Revolution.
en.Q131901869: Atikhisar Castle, or Gavurhisar Castle, is a historic castle thought to date from antiquity, near the central district of Çanakkale. It lies north-east of the Atikhisar Dam, near the village of Kayadere, an area valued for both its nature and its archaeological potential.
en.Q131901984: Turhal Castle in the Turhal district of Tokat is built on a steep rock about 180 m above the plain, commanding both the town and the plain. The Yeşilırmak river flows nearby.
en.Q131902412: Kilye Castle stands on the shore of the Dardanelles, on the right side of the Eceabat–Gelibolu road; part of it lies under the road built over it. The castle is badly ruined: only its tower facing the strait and a small piece of wall running up the slope remain.
en.Q131921801: Namazgâh Mosque is a mosque in the Yıldırım district of Bursa.
en.Q132004025: The Khedive's Mansion, also called Ali Pasha Mansion, is a palace in the middle of Bebek Bay in Beşiktaş, Istanbul. It was built in 1902 by the Italian architect Raimondo D'Aronco as a summer house for Emine Valide Pasha, mother of Khedive Abbas Hilmi Pasha, and now houses Egypt's Consulate General in Istanbul.
en.Q132089426: Doctor Celepoğlu Mansion, or Celepoğlu House, is a mansion in central Kırklareli built in 1908.
en.Q132133895: Fatih Mosque, also called Eski or Küçük Mosque, is a historic Ottoman mosque in the Babaeski district of Kırklareli. The Four-Sided Fountain and the Babaeski Bath stand in front of it.
en.Q132134113: Gülabi Ahmed Pasha Mosque, also called Paşa or Beyazıt Mosque, is a historic Ottoman mosque in central Kırklareli.
en.Q132134114: Kapan Mosque, or Karaca İbrahim Bey Mosque, is a historic Ottoman mosque in central Kırklareli.
en.Q132134224: Köprülü Mehmed Pasha Mosque in Safranbolu, Karabük, is a classical Ottoman mosque built in 1661–1662 by Grand Vizier Köprülü Mehmed Pasha, who began the Köprülü era. One of Safranbolu's most important historic buildings, it forms a complex with the madrasa, library, ablution fountain and bath around it.
en.Q132134367: Çınarlı Mosque, formerly Agia Iorgi Church, is a historic mosque in Ayvalık, Balıkesir, built in 1880. Originally a Greek Orthodox church, it became a mosque in 1923 after the population exchange.
en.Q132134404: Hatuniye Mosque, or the Hatuniye Complex, is in the Şehzadeler district of Manisa. Prince Şehinşah built it in 1490–91 in the name of his mother Hüsnüşah Hatun, wife of Bayezid II. Largely destroyed by an earthquake in 1611, it was rebuilt through repairs during the 17th century.
en.Q132182608: Kulaksızlar Mound, also called the Kulaksızlar marble idol workshop, is a Chalcolithic settlement near the Kulaksızlar quarter of Akhisar, Manisa, where marble was worked and figurines were made.
en.Q132182748: Tepebağ Höyük is a settlement mound in Seyhan, Adana. It has been settled without a break since the Early Bronze Age.
en.Q132195019: Hüdavent Hatun Tomb in Erzurum is the tomb of Hüdavent Hatun, daughter of the Anatolian Seljuk sultan Kılıç Arslan IV. Part of the Çifte Minareli Madrasa (Hatuniye Madrasa) complex, it is the largest kümbet tomb in Erzurum; her grave lies in its lower chamber.
en.Q132655068: Havuz-Aslantaş (Havuz Köy) is a Late Hittite settlement in the village of Havuz in the Kangal district of Sivas.
en.Q132681878: The 25 December Gaziantep Defence Heroism Panorama and Museum tells, through various materials, the story of Gaziantep's defence against British and French occupation during the Turkish War of Independence. It is a certified private museum supervised by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism.
en.Q132682071: The Mimar Sinan and City Museum is in the Recep Tayyip Erdoğan National Garden in Kayseri. It covers the life and works of Mimar Sinan and the historical, natural and cultural heritage of Kayseri. The building, designed through a national architecture competition in 2021, was completed at the end of 2025; an official opening date has not yet been set.
en.Q132682091: The Şanlıurfa Traditional Handicrafts Museum in central Şanlıurfa is an ethnography museum set up to present, keep alive and sell traditional crafts. It displays local crafts from copperwork and kilim weaving to felt-making and woodcarving, and also runs training activities.
en.Q132682113: Denizli City Museum shows the cultural, social and economic heritage of Denizli from prehistory to the present. It opened on 13 March 2024 in the restored stone workshop buildings of the former Şehit Yusuf Batur Vocational High School, a fine example of early Republican architecture.
en.Q132682131: The museum building is the house where Atatürk stayed in Yalova before the Walking Pavilion was built. It was restored in 1981 and opened as a museum displaying his belongings.
en.Q132735498: Değirmendere Bridge is a four-arched bridge over the Değirmendere in the Ortahisar district of Trabzon. With a relief arch on its west side, it is 137 metres long and 5.5 metres wide, and was built in 1891 by the Nemlizade family.
en.Q132735505: Vaniti Bridge is a single-span, flat-decked arch bridge in the Borçka district of Artvin, thought to date from the 18th century. It is 33 m long and 2.9 m wide and stands in the village of Düzköy, hence its other name, Düzköy Vaniti Bridge. Its piers, which have niches, are of rubble stone and its arch of cut stone.
en.Q132735650: Bağlar Bridge, or Nehri Bridge, crosses the Şemdinli stream at Bağlar, Şemdinli (Hakkari).
en.Q132752814: Tuz Han is a historic building in Bursa.
en.Q132752833: Dombaycıoğlu Han is an Ottoman-era trading building in the Akhisar district of Manisa. Built in 1823 by Dombaycıoğlu Mehmet Ağa, it was registered in 1963 and protected as a cultural asset in 1980.
en.Q132752839: El-Aman Han is a historic Ottoman inn on the Rahva Plain in Bitlis, built in 1579 by Hüsrev Pasha to lodge travellers and caravans. Its size and facilities make it look like a caravanserai. The origin of the name El-Aman is not known.
en.Q132752942: Issız Han is a historic inn near the village of Seyran in Karacabey, Bursa. Built at the end of the 14th century, it shows Seljuk-period architectural features.
en.Q132752944: Cinci Han is a historic inn in Safranbolu, built in 1645 by Karabaşzade Hüseyin Efendi.
en.Q132752964: Raziye Sultan Han is the caravanserai in the centre of Kadınhanı, Konya, which gave the town its name.
en.Q132752971: Döğer Caravanserai is an Ottoman caravanserai in the town of Döğer, in the İhsaniye district of Afyonkarahisar.
en.Q132899013: The Bülent Ecevit Museum is in the Kayalıbağ quarter of Adana. It was set up in a historic building restored by Adana Metropolitan Municipality and opened on 20 July 2023, the anniversary of the 1974 Cyprus operation.
en.Q132900662: The Ancient Luwian Culture Centre is a museum on the culture and history of the ancient Luwian people. It opened on 20 June 2023 in the Ulucami quarter of Seyhan, Adana.
en.Q133319341: Karakaş Bey Mosque, or Karakaş Mosque, is in central Kırklareli. The original Ottoman mosque was built in the 17th century; after it was destroyed at an unknown date it was rebuilt in reinforced concrete.
en.Q133539662: The Karahıdır Monument, also called Karahızır or Four Legs Monument, is an Ottoman-era monument in central Kırklareli.
en.Q133683488: This mansion in central Kırklareli, built in 1880, is known as Doctor Kerameas Mansion, Doctor Peterkof's Mansion, the Turkish Hearth Building or the Kırklareli Culture and Art House.
en.Q133698720: The Yaşar Museum is a private museum in the Konak district of İzmir, with collections of painting, archaeology and ethnography. It opened on 17 January 2026 in a former flour mill of 1895 restored by the Yaşar Education and Culture Foundation.
en.Q133817719: Kanuni House (Kanuni Evi) is a history museum in the Ortahisar district of Trabzon.
en.Q133864247: Fatma Hatun Mosque, or Fatma Hatun Mescidi, is in the Vize district of Kırklareli. The original small prayer house is said to date from the first half of the 17th century; local residents rebuilt it as a mosque in 1962.
en.Q134112886: Şeyh Ebul Vefa Mosque is in the Meram district of Konya. It was built by the Karamanid ruler İbrahim Bey in the name of Ebul Vefa.
en.Q134592335: Erikli Waterfall is a natural waterfall near the village of Teşvikiye in the Termal district of Yalova. Its natural beauty and cool air draw visitors especially in summer.
en.Q134706663: Doctor Hacı Yanaki Mansion, or Aydın Akkul House, is a late 19th-century mansion in central Kırklareli.
en.Q134727996: The Great Harbour Monument is an impressive 1st-century BC marble structure on the southwest pier of the Lion Harbour in ancient Miletus. Probably built to celebrate a naval victory of the Milesian fleet, it stands in front of the western wing of the Harbour Stoa.
en.Q134961438: The Russian Monument in Gelibolu was unveiled on 16 July 1921 by the 'White Russians' in memory of their fallen comrades. It stands in the Gazi Süleyman Paşa quarter and can be reached by following the signs from the town entrance.
en.Q134978988: Gelibolu Martyrs' Cemetery is a military cemetery in the Gelibolu district of Çanakkale.
en.Q135629383: Ali Kuşçu Mosque, formerly Istanbul Airport Mosque, is a mosque near Istanbul Airport in the Arnavutköy district. It opened on 14 June 2020 and, including its courtyard, has room for 6,230 worshippers. It is named after the astronomer Ali Kuşçu.
en.Q135913465: Celal Karakaş Mosque is a mosque inside the Hamitler City Cemetery in the Hamitler quarter of Osmangazi, Bursa.
en.Q136462676: Özlüce Church of St George stands on the village square of Özlüce in Nilüfer, Bursa. It was built in the early 20th century as a Greek Orthodox church and, as of 2025, is used as a mosque.
en.Q137507481: Sülüklü Mosque (Süluki Mosque) is a mosque in the Doğanbey quarter of Osmangazi, Bursa, originally built in the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent.
en.Q137584527: Asiye Hatun Mosque in Safranbolu was built by Asiye Hatun in 1939.
en.Q137637960: Mustafapaşa Cami-i Kebir (Mustafapaşa Great Mosque) is an Ottoman mosque in the centre of Mustafapaşa, Ürgüp (Nevşehir).
en.Q137774229: The Tomb of Pir Sücaeddin İlyas, also called Yukarı Pirler Tomb, stands in Pirler Park south of Çilehane Mosque in Amasya. It was built in 1486 by Gümüşlüzade Ahmet Bey in memory of Sheikh Pir Sücaeddin İlyas. It also holds the graves of his son-in-law Pir Celaleddin Abdurrahman, his grandson Pir Hayreddin Hızır Çelebi and their families.
en.Q137787535: The Church of Constantine and Helena is an 18th-century church, partly built and partly carved into rock, on the square of Mustafapaşa, Ürgüp (Nevşehir).
en.Q139419209: Şarkışla Castle, also called Atatürk Castle or, in scholarly sources, Şarkışla Central Mound, is a historic defensive structure and archaeological mound in the centre of Şarkışla, Sivas, on a conical hill at about 1,250 metres.
en.Q140389754: The Serindere Waterfalls are six separate falls in the Serindere Canyon, which runs between the Başiskele and Kartepe districts of Kocaeli.
en.Q141064290: Kayacı Valley, or Lamas Canyon, is a valley and natural area near Limonlu in the Erdemli district of Mersin. Shaped by the Limonlu (Lamos) stream, it is known for its canyon landscape, riverside vegetation, biodiversity and historic remains.
en.Q1496350: Hacınebi Mound lies north-west of Şanlıurfa, 5 km north of Birecik, beside the village of Uğurcuk (Hacınebi). It stands where the Euphrates bends east, at a crossing of trade routes from Mesopotamia to Central Anatolia along the river valley. It measures 240 x 140 metres.
en.Q15056847: İsa Bey Bath, or the Great Bath, is an old hamam in Selçuk, İzmir.
en.Q15076283: Safa Mosque, also known as Parlı Mosque, is a historic mosque in the Sur district of Diyarbakır. It is also called Şeyh Safa, İpariye, İparla and Palo.
en.Q1507787: Yeni Rabat Church, or Akhaldaba Church, is a medieval Georgian church in the Çamlık quarter of Bulanık village in the Ardanuç district of Artvin, in the historic Klarjeti region. Most sources call it Yeni Rabat Church, but an old source names it Akhaldaba.
en.Q15078111: Vialand, formerly İsfanbul, was the first theme park built in Türkiye. It lies in the Yeşilpınar quarter where Istanbul's Eyüpsultan and Gaziosmanpaşa districts meet, and opened on 26 May 2013. Besides the theme park it has a shopping centre and a hotel.
en.Q16008767: The Church of Surp Asdvadzadzin is an Armenian church in Beşiktaş, Istanbul. Built in masonry in 1838 by the court architect Garabed Amira Balyan, it was renewed in 1987 under Patriarch Shnork I; busts of Garabed and Sarkis Balyan were placed in its courtyard in 1993. Renovated in 2013, it is the burial place of Artin Dadyan Pasha.
en.Q1616641: Troy Historical National Park is a national park in Çanakkale, Türkiye.
en.Q16365061: Ardanuç Castle is a medieval Georgian castle in the town of Ardanuç, Artvin, in the historic Klarjeti region. Turkish sources also call it Gevhernik Castle, a name probably from the Persian "Gevher-i Nik", meaning "fine jewel".
en.Q16371936: Mamatzminda Church is a medieval Georgian church in the village of İbrikli, formerly Ebrika, in the Borçka district of Artvin, in the historic Klarjeti region. It is also called İbrikli Church after the village's present name.
en.Q1653170: Uçmakdere is a neighbourhood in the Şarköy district of Tekirdağ.
en.Q17138662: The Nezahat Gökyiğit Botanic Garden (NGBB) is a botanic garden in the Ataşehir district of Istanbul. The ANG Foundation founded it in 1995 in the name of Nezahat Gökyiğit, wife of Ali Nihat Gökyiğit. First a memorial park, it became a botanic garden and opened to visitors in 2003.
en.Q1738167: Kelenderis is an ancient city of Rough Cilicia in today's Aydıncık district of Mersin. Excavations began in 1987.
en.Q17471848: The Gazi Mustafa Kemal Monument, dedicated to Atatürk, stands on Cumhuriyet Square in the Silifke district of Mersin.
en.Q1765238: Lidar Höyük is a settlement mound 23 km north of Bozova, northwest of Şanlıurfa. It lay partly under and partly southwest of Lidar village, which is now under the waters of the Atatürk Dam lake. Its name is thought to come from Ltar Castle, mentioned in Byzantine documents.
en.Q1785613: Lake Kovada is a small freshwater lake in Isparta, north of the Gulf of Antalya, in the Lakes Region. It lies on a north–south fault and is a natural extension of Lake Eğirdir; excess water from Lake Eğirdir flows into it through a canal.
en.Q18087897: İskender Baba Lodge, or Kaymakçı Lodge, is an Ottoman-era dervish lodge in the Ahmediye quarter of Üsküdar, Istanbul. It was built by the Janissary officer Mehmet Efendi; work began in 1544 and it opened the same year.
en.Q18155881: Jonah's Pillar (Yunus Sütunu) is a historic ruin in the Sarıseki quarter of İskenderun, Hatay, where the impassable Sarıseki canyon meets the Mediterranean. Little more than neglected piles of stone remains. Locals believe this is where the prophet Jonah came ashore from the belly of the fish, hence the name.
en.Q18674546: Ortaköy Bath, or Hüsrev Kethüda Bath, is a historic building in Ortaköy, Istanbul.
en.Q18681409: The Tomb of Abdal Mehmet is a 15th-century building in the Demirtaş quarter of Osmangazi, Bursa.
en.Q18713516: Acıgöl is a volcanic maar lake in the Karapınar district of Konya, on the Karapınar plain north-east of Meke Crater Lake, at kilometre 8 of the Karapınar–Ereğli road. The elliptical lake lies at 988 m, measures 1,750 by 1,250 m and covers 1.2 km².
en.Q18868213: Mount Ararat National Park was declared in 2004 over 88,014 hectares around Mount Ararat. It is known for the story of Noah's flood, Türkiye's highest mountain and largest glacier, a meteor crater and its varied wildlife.
en.Q18917029: The Armenian Church of Surp Nigoğayos was built in Samsun, then in the Canik sanjak, in 1840 or 1849 and belonged to the Armenian Apostolic Church. It no longer exists.
en.Q18917052: The Holy Trinity (Aya Triada) Greek Orthodox Church was built in Samsun in the Ottoman period and belonged to the Ecumenical Patriarchate.
en.Q195876: The Ani Bridge, or Silk Road Bridge, is a 9th-century stone bridge over the Arpaçay river on the border between Türkiye and Armenia. It stands where the historic Silk Road first entered Anatolia; one abutment is in Türkiye and the other in Armenia. It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2016 as part of the Archaeological Site of Ani.
en.Q19610433: Constitution Square (Anayasa Meydanı) is on the shore of the Gulf of İzmir in Karşıyaka, east of the Karşıyaka ferry pier. Its main feature is the Atatürk, His Mother and Women's Rights Monument, and it is used for ceremonies and public events.
en.Q19610508: Amisos Hill, formerly Baruthane Hill, is on the Samsun–Sinop road 4 km from the city centre. The site, dating from the 3rd century BC, was discovered on 28 November 1995. Its tumulus tombs had been found and robbed by treasure hunters before they were protected, so parts of them are damaged.
en.Q19610585: The Atatürk Forest Farm Zoo was set up in 1933 inside the Atatürk Forest Farm to show animals harmful to farming and people. As it drew great public interest, Atatürk instructed the agriculture minister Muhsin Erkmen to build a modern, well-organised zoo.
en.Q19611037: The Dur Yolcu (Stop, Traveller) Monument is at Kilitbahir in Eceabat, Çanakkale. It was created in 1960 on the initiative of a group of soldiers, who wrote the first lines of the poem 'Bir Yolcuya' by Necmettin Halil Onan on the hillside. It was renewed in 2019 by the Historical Site Directorate.
en.Q19611082: Lake Efteni is a freshwater lake of tectonic origin on the border of the central and Gölyaka districts of Düzce, 10 km south-west of Düzce and 2 km east of Gölyaka. In 2005 a 76-hectare wildlife development area was established around the lake.
en.Q19611962: Merzifon Çelebi Mehmet Madrasa, also called Sultaniye Madrasa, was built in 1414–1415 by Ebu Bekr b. Muhammed el-Müşeymeş on the order of the Ottoman sultan Mehmed I. It is in the centre of Merzifon, right next to Çelebi Mehmet Madrasa Mosque. Its first teacher was Ferîdüddîn-i Dîvânî.
en.Q19612437: Sekibaşı Mosque is a 19th-century Ottoman mosque in Muğla.
en.Q19612520: Sofular Mosque, also called Abdullah Pasha Mosque, is in the centre of Merzifon. It was built in 1501 by Abdullah Pasha, governor-general.
en.Q19612665: Lake Taşkısığı (Çaltıcak Lake) is a 90-hectare spring-fed freshwater lake in the Adapazarı district of Sakarya, 15 km from the centre at an altitude of 15 metres. It is protected as a wetland, and a 444-hectare area around it was placed under protection on 30 December 2022.
en.Q19612689: The Tekkeköy Caves Archaeology Valley Museum House is in the Tekkeköy district of Samsun, in the valley of the Tekkeköy Caves, the earliest human settlement in the Black Sea region. It was created by restoring one of three registered old Greek houses in the area.
en.Q19613015: Yahşihan Iron Bridge, or Abdulhamid Bridge, crosses the Kızılırmak on the road to Bedesten village in the Yahşihan district of Kırıkkale. Built by Sultan Abdulhamid II, it is Türkiye's first iron bridge.
en.Q19613310: Çanakkale TV Tower is a television and observation tower on Radar Tepe, at an altitude of 312 metres. The tower is 98 metres tall and has a culture centre and a restaurant. Its design was chosen through an international competition, and the construction tender was held in 2016.
en.Q19613323: The Old Rock Mosque of Çavuşin is a mosque in the village of Çavuşin, Avanos (Nevşehir).
en.Q19737976: The Zeki Müren Art Museum is in the Bodrum district of Muğla. The house where the Turkish classical music singer Zeki Müren spent the last years of his life was rearranged by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism and opened to visitors on 8 July 2000.
en.Q19802324: Nemrut Mountain National Park spans the provinces of Adıyaman and Malatya. It covers Mount Nemrut and its surroundings, including an archaeological site in the Kâhta district with an ancient city of the Kingdom of Commagene. It is reached by road from Adıyaman via Kâhta, and Adıyaman airport is nearby.
en.Q2031691: Ortakent Yahşi is a neighbourhood in the Bodrum district of Muğla.
en.Q20470457: Hoca Ahmed Fakih Mosque is a 13th-century Seljuk mosque and complex in the Meram district of Konya.
en.Q20470665: Kütahya Great Mosque, also known as Yıldırım Beyazıt Mosque, is the only imperial mosque in Kütahya. It was begun when Prince Bayezid (Yıldırım) was governor of Kütahya (1381–1389) and completed by his son Prince Musa Çelebi after Bayezid was captured at the Battle of Ankara.
en.Q20470671: Çinili Mosque in Kütahya was built by the painter Ahmet Yakupoğlu and opened for worship in 1975. Covered inside and out with Kütahya tiles, it has become one of the city's symbols.
en.Q20470812: The Atatürk Congress and Culture Centre (Merinos AKKM) is a congress and culture complex of two buildings inside Merinos Park, Bursa.
en.Q20470876: Samsun City Museum in the İlkadım district opened on 12 February 2013. It displays information and objects on Samsun's social, historical, cultural, geographical and economic life. It drew 20,000 visitors in its first seventy days and received a special jury award from the Union of Historic Towns.
en.Q20470881: Avlan Lake is a karst lake in the Elmalı district of Antalya, 1,030 m above sea level and 850 hectares in its natural state. With Karagöl it lies in the Elmalı Polje, 1,030–1,050 m high, between Elmalı Mountain and the Bey Mountains. The lake formed in the lowest part of the limestone polje.
en.Q20470923: The Church of St Demetrius (Aya Dimitri) is a Greek Orthodox church in Kurtuluş (Tatavla), Istanbul. Its courtyard holds a cemetery used until 1865. The church is open for worship every day.
en.Q20471219: The Sultan Dîvânî Mevlevi Lodge Museum, formerly the Afyonkarahisar Mevlevi Lodge, is an old Mevlevi dervish lodge in Afyonkarahisar. Today it serves as a museum.
en.Q20471257: The Church of Surp Garabet is an Armenian church in Üsküdar, Istanbul. Built before 1593, it was renewed in 1617 and 1727 and repaired in 1844. It burned down in 1887 and was rebuilt in masonry in 1888. After repairs in 2006 it was reopened by the Armenian Patriarch of Istanbul, Mesrob II.
en.Q20471279: The Church of Surp Haç is an Armenian church in Üsküdar, Istanbul. The first church here was built in 1689, rebuilt in 1727 on the orders of Patriarch Hovhannes IX Golod, and repaired several times between 1779 and 1808.
en.Q20471314: This chapel is in Balıklı Armenian Cemetery, an Armenian Apostolic cemetery in the Seyitnizam quarter of Zeytinburnu, Istanbul. The cemetery is named after Balıklı, once a separate settlement and now part of Zeytinburnu, and is maintained by the Armenian Patriarchate of Türkiye.
en.Q20471335: The Church of Surp Vartanants is an Armenian church in Feriköy, Şişli (Istanbul). Begun in 1859 and opened in 1861, it was repaired in 1903, rebuilt in masonry in 1929 and opened in 1931 by Patriarch Mesrob I Naroyan. It was repaired again in 2006 and 2011.
en.Q20471356: The Church of Surp Yeyğa is an Armenian church in the Eyüpsultan district of Istanbul. The 18th-century church was demolished in 1766 but reopened in 1800; it was rebuilt in 1832 and renewed in 1851. After its last repair in 2000 it was reopened by Patriarch Mesrob II.
en.Q20471532: Kapu Mosque is a 17th-century Ottoman mosque on Sarraflar Street in the Meram district of Konya, the largest of the city's Ottoman mosques. It belongs to the General Directorate of Foundations and is in use for worship.
en.Q20471536: Balık Gölü (Fish Lake) is a coastal lagoon lake in the Kızılırmak Delta, Samsun.
en.Q20471575: Mudanya Tahir Pasha Mansion City Museum has occupied an 18th-century mansion in Mudanya since 2013.
en.Q20471785: Karasu Castle is a 12th–13th-century Byzantine castle in the Karasu district of Sakarya, built of rough natural stone with lime mortar. It stands south-west of Tuzla village on the bank of the Sakarya river; only a small foundation wall remains.
en.Q20472190: Kayseri Clock Tower stands on Cumhuriyet Square in Kayseri. It was built in 1906 on the orders of Sultan Abdulhamid II.
en.Q20472206: The Church of Surp Nigoğayos is an Armenian Apostolic church in the Beykoz district of Istanbul.
en.Q20472639: Kırıkkale Nur Mosque is a mosque in Kırıkkale. The architect Necip Dinç designed the mosque and all the units of its complex; the first design of the mufti's office and the bazaar was by Mükremin Karakoç, and Dinç designed their exteriors to match the classical style of the mosque.
en.Q20473289: Boğazköy-Alacahöyük Historical National Park is a protected area of 2,600 hectares in the Boğazkale district of Çorum, established in 1988.
en.Q20473482: Geyve Han is an inn in the Grand Bazaar of Bursa, built in the 15th century by Hacı İvaz Pasha, son of Ahi Bayezıt of the Tokat Akhis, to provide income for the Green Mosque, and presented to Mehmed I. It was formerly known as Hacı İvaz Pasha Han, Payigâh, Lonca and Ütücüler Han.
en.Q20473521: Nene Hatun National Park is in central Erzurum.
en.Q20473700: The Bandırma Ferry and National Struggle Park Open-Air Museum is in the Canik district of Samsun. It opened on 18 May 2003 as the Bandırma Ferry Museum.
en.Q20474003: Abdülmecid Efendi Pavilion is a historic pavilion in Bağlarbaşı Grove, Kuzguncuk (Istanbul).
en.Q20474440: Uçansu Waterfall is in the village of Akçapınar near Gebiz, in the Serik district of Antalya, 57 km from Antalya and 54 km from Serik. It lies 38 km from the sea as the crow flies, 400 m above sea level. The upper fall drops 70 m and the lower fall 51.5 m. After Gebiz the road is gravel and can be impassable in spring when the water rises.
en.Q20474472: Harmantepe Castle is a Byzantine castle near the village of Harmantepe in the Söğütlü district of Sakarya. It was built in the 12th or 13th century to defend the eastern border of the Byzantine Empire.
en.Q20474544: Valla Canyon is in the village of Muratbaşı (Valla), Pınarbaşı (Kastamonu), inside Küre Mountains National Park. Cut by the Devrekani stream through the Küre Mountains, it is 12 km long and, at 800 m deep, one of the deepest canyons in Türkiye.
en.Q20476230: The Ali Fuat Pasha Kuva-yi Milliye Museum is in the Alifuatpaşa quarter of Geyve, Sakarya. It displays belongings of Ali Fuat Cebesoy, a commander in the War of Independence, and of the Kuva-yi Milliye forces.
en.Q20476315: All Saints Church in Moda, also known as the Istanbul Presbyterian Church, is home to a Presbyterian congregation.
en.Q20476316: Sadrettin Konevi Mosque is a 13th-century Seljuk mosque in Konya.
en.Q20476707: Serbostani Mustafa Ağa Mosque, or Beykoz Central Mosque, is a historic mosque on the central shore of Beykoz. It was built in 1809 and renewed in 2006.
en.Q20476815: The Tomb of Çoban Bey is on the street named after him in the Mollaarap quarter of Bursa. It belongs to Çoban Bey, one of the sons of Osman Bey, founder of the Ottoman Empire, and holds five sarcophagi including his. It has no inscription, but foundation records show it was built in the early 14th century.
en.Q20476828: The Dzınunt Surp Asdvadzadzni Church is an Armenian Orthodox church in Zeytinlik, Bakırköy (Istanbul).
en.Q20476974: Yeniçağa Lake is a tectonic lake near Yeniçağa, Bolu, formed under the influence of the North Anatolian Fault. It covers 2.6 km² at 989 m above sea level. Its fresh water is 11 m deep at most and about 5 m on average. The lake is 7 km long and 2.5 km wide.
en.Q20476987: The Yerevman Surp Haç Church is an Armenian church in Kuruçeşme, Beşiktaş (Istanbul). Built in 1798, it was repaired by Garabed Amira Balyan in 1834; in 1835 Harutyun Amira Yerganyan built the Tarkmançats Armenian Primary School next to it. It was repaired again in 1975 and 1988.
en.Q20477010: The Church of Surp Stepanos is an Armenian church in Yeşilköy, Bakırköy (Istanbul). It was built on the site of an earlier church in 1826 by the chief gunpowder maker Simon Amira Dadyan, rebuilt in 1843 and opened in 1844 by Patriarch Asdvadzadur II. It was last repaired in 2000 and reopened by Patriarch Mesrob II.
en.Q20477232: Santa Maria Catholic Church is in the Ortahisar district of Trabzon. The complex of the church, a guesthouse and two outbuildings was built between 1869 and 1874. The three-aisled basilica has a tiled barrel vault and many icons and frescoes inside.
en.Q20477249: Şeyh Mosque is a 16th-century Ottoman mosque in Muğla.
en.Q20643714: Beştepe Millet Mosque is a mosque for 3,000 worshippers in the Presidential Complex in Beştepe, Yenimahalle, Ankara, where the Presidential Palace stands. It opened for worship on 3 July 2015, just before Friday prayers.
en.Q20728661: Zazadin Han is a 13th-century Anatolian Seljuk caravanserai near the Selçuklu district of Konya, on the Konya–Aksaray road about 22 km from the city centre.
en.Q2085773: Philadelphia (Greek Φιλαδέλφεια) was a city in the interior of western Anatolia, within ancient Lydia and in the Katakekaumene area, and one of the ten cities of a local Decapolis.
en.Q21201418: The Surp Pırgiç Armenian Hospital Chapel is an Armenian church in Kazlıçeşme, Zeytinburnu (Istanbul), within the Yedikule Surp Pırgiç Armenian Hospital complex. Opened in 1834, it was designed by Hovhannes Amira Serveryan and the court architect Garabed Amira Balyan; when it fell into disrepair it was renewed in 1906 to designs by Krikor Melidosyan and Yeğiazar Avedisyan.
en.Q21288238: The Walking Pavilion (Yürüyen Köşk) is a rectangular, two-storey, part-masonry pavilion built in 1929 on the Yalova National Farm.
en.Q21523662: Lake Gölcük is an alluvial-dam lake in the Gölcük quarter of Ödemiş, İzmir, 5 km from the town of Bozdağ. The lake covers 0.941 km² and is up to 7 m deep; the surrounding 1,521-hectare area, home to various trees, plants and forests, was placed under protection on 30 December 2022.
en.Q21523718: Orhan Mosque in central Adapazarı was built in the name of Orhan Gazi. It is a rectangular mosque of cut stone.
en.Q21523968: Akçakoca Clock Tower in Akçakoca, Düzce, was created in 1954 when a clock was added to the minaret of the old Akçakoca Central Mosque. The original minaret design is preserved: narrow edges, an octagonal plan and a lead-covered dome.
en.Q21524010: Amasya Clock Tower stands in the central district of Amasya. Built in 1865 by Ziya Pasha, the district governor, it was damaged by a fire that same year and badly hit by the 1938 earthquake. It was pulled down in February 1940 to build a new bridge, and rebuilt true to the original in 2002.
en.Q21524173: Bahadın Clock Tower is in the town of Bahadın, Sorgun (Yozgat). Inspired by the Yozgat Clock Tower, it has a square shaft, a pavilion with twin windows and a pointed dome. Its date is unknown.
en.Q21524214: Bayburt Clock Tower stands in the central district of Bayburt. Its clocks first ran on 29 October 1924. It was inspired by clock towers that Bayburt's soldiers had seen while fighting elsewhere during the War of Independence, and its style resembles Çorum Clock Tower. On a round base, the shaft is octagonal and the top square.
en.Q21524488: Bozcaada Clock Tower in Çanakkale was created in 1897 when a clock was added to the bell tower of the Church of St Mary. It is 28 metres tall.
en.Q21524555: Burdur Clock Tower stands in the central district of Burdur. The original tower, put up in 1830 or 1836, collapsed in the 1914 earthquake; the present tower was rebuilt on the same spot in 1937.
en.Q21524994: Dikilitaş is a Roman monument in the İznik district of Bursa, also called Beştaş or Nişantaşı. It stands among olive groves in the village of Elbeyli, on the old Roman road between İznik (Nicaea) and İzmit (Nicomedia), 7 km north of İznik.
en.Q21526100: Gerede Clock Tower stands on Cumhuriyet Square in Gerede, Bolu. It was put up in 1882, is made of pine wood and is 12 metres high.
en.Q21526339: Karabük Clock Tower stands in central Karabük. It was erected for the 50th anniversary of the Kardemir steelworks and completed on 3 April 1987, with a polygonal shaft.
en.Q21526366: Kastamonu Clock Tower is a cut-stone tower about 12 metres tall in central Kastamonu. Its 1.6-metre dial with Eastern Arabic numerals is said to have been sent by Abdulhamid II. It was last restored in 2002.
en.Q21526451: The Konya Atatürk Monument, the second Atatürk monument in the Republic after the one at Sarayburnu, was made in 1926 by the Austrian sculptor Heinrich Krippel. It stands on Government Square on İstasyon Street in Konya.
en.Q21526471: Kurtalan Clock Tower in the Kurtalan district of Siirt was built by the municipality in 1999. It has three storeys and a round dial.
en.Q21526473: Kuruçeşme is a neighbourhood of İzmit.
en.Q21526496: Kütahya Clock Tower stands in central Kütahya.
en.Q21526530: Maden Clock Tower is a historic clock tower in the Maden district of Elazığ, built in 1898 next to the government building by District Governor Hayri Bey. Its eaves and dome collapsed and its inscription and clock were lost; it was faithfully restored in 2018.
en.Q21526554: Manisa Clock Tower in the Şehzadeler district was created in 1672 when a clock was added over the projecting north entrance of Manisa Great Mosque (completed in 1366). If the 1672 date is right, it was the first clock tower in Türkiye. It survived the great Manisa fire of 1922, but the clock structure was later completely demolished.
en.Q21526567: The Marmara Theology Mosque (in full, the Marmara University Faculty of Theology Abdullah Tivnikli Practice Mosque and Culture Centre) is a mosque and culture centre in Üsküdar, Istanbul.
en.Q21526615: Mersin Clock Tower in the Akdeniz district of Mersin is part of the Mersin Catholic Church, begun in 1853 and completed in 1898, and also serves as its bell tower.
en.Q21526655: Mudurnu Clock Tower is a wood-clad clock tower with a tiled roof in Mudurnu, Bolu.
en.Q21526882: Safranbolu Clock Tower in Karabük province was built in 1797 by İzzet Mehmed Pasha as the first known clock tower in Anatolia. The square, cut-stone tower is 20 metres tall, and its original clock, brought from London, still works.
en.Q21526912: Lake Sarıkum is a shallow, slightly salty lagoon lake on the west side of the Sinop Peninsula, formed when a coastal bar closed off an old bay.
en.Q21526984: Siirt Clock Tower stands east of Siirt Great Mosque in central Siirt. The original tower, built by Alaaddin Pasha in 1905, eventually collapsed; the present one was built in 1975.
en.Q21526998: Singeç Bridge is a bridge in the Pertek district of Tunceli.
en.Q21527012: Sivrihisar Clock Tower in the Sivrihisar district of Eskişehir was built in 1900 by District Governor Mahmud Bey and Mayor Yüzügüllü Hacı Mehmet Efendi. It is 12 metres tall. Its bell was stolen in December 2006 but was found in Afyonkarahisar in 2007 and put back.
en.Q21527049: Sungurlu Clock Tower stands in the Sungurlu district of Çorum. It was built in 1891 or 1892 by master builder Şakir of Yozgat and served as a model for the Yozgat and Çorum clock towers. It is 19 metres tall.
en.Q21527099: Taşhan in central Bolu is a group of late Ottoman inns built of cut stone. They draw attention for their look and are used today as a book-trade centre.
en.Q21527119: Tepsi Minaret, also called Kesik Kule or Erzurum Clock Tower, is in the Yakutiye district of Erzurum. It began as the minaret of a small mosque built by Ebu'l-Muzaffer Gazi, who ruled from 1124 to 1132. The exact date the clock was added is unknown, but it was before 1843.
en.Q21527137: Tokat Clock Tower stands in central Tokat.
en.Q21527288: Vezirköprü Clock Tower is in the Vezirköprü district of Samsun. The original tower of 1908 was badly damaged in the 1943 earthquake and rebuilt faithfully to the original in 1959.
en.Q21527391: Zile Castle stands on a mound in the centre of Zile, overlooking the Zile plain. Roman and Byzantine architectural pieces and inscriptions found in and around it suggest it was built in the 1st century AD.
en.Q21527403: Çanakkale Clock Tower stands near the ferry pier in central Çanakkale. It was built in 1896 by District Governor Cemil Pasha with funding from Vitalis Gaptiorele, and is a five-storey tower 20 metres tall.
en.Q21527407: Çankırı Clock Tower stands in central Çankırı. The first clock tower on this spot was built in 1869; the present tower, put up in 1901, was moved to its current location in 1948.
en.Q21528301: Çerikli Clock Tower is in the town of Çerikli, Delice (Kırıkkale), and is the only clock tower in Kırıkkale province. Modelled on the İzmir Clock Tower, it was erected in 1991 in the park on Çerikli's Cumhuriyet Square.
en.Q21528347: Ürgüp Clock Tower in the Ürgüp district of Nevşehir was built in 2006 by MİAR Architecture under the Ürgüp Urban Rehabilitation Plan. The square prism tower recalls Cappadocia's fairy chimneys and has reliefs on all four sides.
en.Q21528431: Şanlıurfa Clock Tower in the Eyyübiye district was created by adding a clock, sometime between 1927 and 1945, to the 30-metre minaret of Şanlıurfa Great Mosque, completed in 1175.
en.Q21528438: The Martyrs' Clock Tower, or Niksar Clock Tower, is in the Niksar district of Tokat. Built in 2008 by Mayor İdris Şahin, it bears the names of people from Niksar who died in the War of Independence and scenes from the war.
en.Q21541477: Kaçkar Mountains National Park lies mostly in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize, extending into Erzurum and Artvin provinces. The 51,550-hectare park covers the Kaçkar Mountains between the Fırtına and Hemşin streams.
en.Q21681864: 50. Yıl Park is a park in the Çankaya district of Ankara.
en.Q2225271: Sarıhan Caravanserai is on the Aksaray–Kayseri section of the Silk Road in Nevşehir province, in the Damsa valley 5 km south-east of Avanos and 6 km north of Ürgüp. Built in 1249 in the reign of (and perhaps by) Kaykaus II, it covers 2,000 m².
en.Q22977153: St Paul's Church is a historic Roman Catholic church in the Meram district of Konya. It is named after the apostle Paul, who came to Iconium (Konya) on his first missionary journey in Anatolia.
en.Q2368617: Surp Haç Tıbrevank Armenian High School is a high school in Üsküdar. It was first opened in 1678 as a religious school attached to the Church of Surp Haç, and had 102 students as of 2021.
en.Q2397604: Tavşan Island is an island in the Didim district of Aydın, 150 metres west of Tavşan Burnu. Since 2006 the German Archaeological Institute (DAI) has been excavating it as part of its Didyma project, mostly on the south and east sides.
en.Q24040718: Rumeli Feneri Castle, or Topçu Castle, is a 17th-century castle on the hills of Rumelifeneri, Istanbul. It is named after the Rumeli Lighthouse next to it, which also gave the village its name, and is reached by road through Rumelifeneri village in Sarıyer.
en.Q24680949: Heva is a mountain on the border between Georgia and Türkiye, within the Shuakhevi municipality of the Autonomous Republic of Adjara. The summit of the Shavsheti range, it rises 2,812 metres above sea level and holds the sources of the Chirukhistskali and Imerkhevi streams. It is a volcanic mountain with traces of glaciers.
en.Q25472223: Atatürk City Square is a square in the Efeler district of Aydın, built by Aydın Metropolitan Municipality and opened on 15 March 2014. The district's only city square, it has Türkiye's largest water-show pool, an event area for 35,000 people, an Atatürk statue, a martyrs' monument, five cafés, a playground and a car park.
en.Q25472339: Germiyan Church is a former church in Değirmenköy, in the Silivri district of Istanbul.
en.Q25472368: Fatih Pasha Mosque, also known as Kurşunlu Mosque and Bıyıklı Mehmed Pasha Mosque, is a mosque in Diyarbakır. It was built between 1516 and 1520 by Bıyıklı Mehmed Pasha, the city's first Ottoman governor.
en.Q25472378: The Church of St Theodore Tyron (Greek Αγίων Θεοδώρων) is a Greek Orthodox church in the Derinkuyu district of Nevşehir.
en.Q25472424: The Atatürk Mask is a concrete relief of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk's face in Antalya. After two postponements it opened on 10 November 2008, the 70th anniversary of Atatürk's death. Painted gold, it is made of cement, iron and sand. It is 35 metres high and 25 metres wide, making it Türkiye's third-tallest statue.
en.Q25472534: Mount Melendiz is a volcanic mountain north-west of Niğde, between Niğde and Bor. To the west it joins Hasandağı (3,268 m), a young volcanic cone in the same volcanic chain; Hasandağı has a crater vent, Melendiz does not. There are many climbing routes up Melendiz.
en.Q25472559: Büyükesence Orhan Mosque in the Erenler district of Sakarya is built with the çantı (log-notching) technique and is an original example of early Ottoman architecture.
en.Q25474025: The Church of Surp Andon is an Armenian Catholic church in Tarabya, Sarıyer (Istanbul), on Haziran-1 Street. It was built in 1871 by Andon Tıngır Yaver Pasha on land he had bought, and is dedicated to St Anthony.
en.Q25474039: The Church of Surp Levon is an Armenian Catholic church in the Kadıköy district of Istanbul.
en.Q25474071: Osmaniye Clock Tower in central Osmaniye was built in 1998–1999. It is a three-storey square prism tower standing on four legs.
en.Q25474124: The Church of Surp Asdvadzadzin Verapokhum is an Armenian Catholic church on Büyükada, Istanbul. Built under a sultan's decree of 1 November 1856, it was opened by Andon Ağa Apelyan in 1858 on the Feast of the Assumption, and restored in 1956 and 1985.
en.Q25474761: Taşbaşı Church in Ordu was built in 1853 as the Greek Orthodox Church of the Hypapante; the Psomiadis Greek School nearby dates from 1878.
en.Q25474782: The Church of the Taxiarchs (Tahsiarhis) is a Greek Orthodox church in the Arnavutköy quarter of Istanbul.
en.Q25474853: Odunpazarı Modern Museum (OMM) is a museum among the historic Odunpazarı houses of Eskişehir.
en.Q25475745: The Çoban Mustafa Pasha Complex is a 16th-century Ottoman complex on Bağdat Street, Şeftali Sokak, in central Gebze, Kocaeli. It is thought, though not certain, to be the work of Mimar Sinan.
en.Q25475872: Bergama Kurşunlu Mosque is a historic mosque in the Bergama district of İzmir, completed in 1439.
en.Q25475874: Bergama Great Mosque, or Yıldırım Mosque, is a historic mosque in the Bergama district of İzmir, built in 1399 by Sultan Bayezid I (Yıldırım).
en.Q25477115: Çukurova University 57th Regiment Martyrs Mosque is a mosque in Adana, next to the university's Faculty of Theology. It opened for worship in 2021.
en.Q25477141: The Church of Agios Nikolaos is a Greek Orthodox church on Heybeliada (Halki), one of the Princes' Islands of Istanbul.
en.Q25477410: Fatih Mosque in the Foça district of İzmir is named after its founder, Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror.
en.Q25478703: Domuztepe Mound lies 35 km south-east of Osmaniye on the shore of the Aslantaş Dam; its prehistoric levels are now under water.
en.Q26721641: The Seljuk Hunting Lodge stands in the forest at the Kemer turn-off of the Antalya–Kumluca road and dates from 1230–1248. It is one of three known Seljuk hunting lodges and the only Seljuk building in the area, the region's only example of the Turkish-Islamic art tradition.
en.Q28375645: Taşlıkburnu Lighthouse, also called Gelidonya Lighthouse, stands on Cape Gelidonya in the Kumluca district of Antalya.
en.Q29950645: Cebeci Military Cemetery is a public cemetery in the Cebeci quarter of Ankara for soldiers who died fighting for, or gave distinguished service in, the Turkish Armed Forces, and others buried with special permission.
en.Q305501: Abant Lake is a landslide-dammed lake in the Mudurnu district of Bolu, 35 km southwest of Bolu at about 1,350 m. It covers 125 hectares, has fresh water and is 18 m deep at its deepest. The lake and its surroundings became Türkiye's 48th national park on 9 June 2022.
en.Q31187880: Gömeç Hatun Tomb is a 13th-century tomb in Anatolian Seljuk style in the Musalla Cemetery, Konya.
en.Q31188243: Karagöl is a landslide-dammed lake 25 km north of Şavşat, Artvin.
en.Q31188256: A seaside area of Bartın municipality, famous for İnkumu beach.
en.Q31188348: The Kadıköy French Church, or Notre-Dame de l'Assomption, is a neoclassical Catholic church in the Kadıköy district of Istanbul. Designed by Giovanni Battista Barberini, it was completed in 1865. Services are held in French and Turkish.
en.Q31188616: Aya Yorgi Church, or Agios Georgios Church, is a Greek Orthodox church in the Osmaneli district of Bilecik.
en.Q31188685: Kayalar Mosque is a mosque in the Foça district of İzmir.
en.Q31188726: Abdullah Pasha Fountain in the Gülbahar Hatun quarter of Trabzon was built in 1844 by the governor of Trabzon, Hazinedarzade Abdullah Pasha.
en.Q31188734: Hamidiye Mosque in the Konak district of İzmir is named after its founder, Sultan Abdulhamid II.
en.Q31188758: Samsun Bedesten, or Süleyman Pasha Arasta, is a historic covered market in the İlkadım district of Samsun.
en.Q31188759: Boğazköy Museum (Boğazkale Museum) is in the centre of Boğazkale, 82 km south-west of Çorum. It mainly displays finds from the Hittite period.
en.Q31188834: Mencilis Cave, in the village of Bulak in Karabük province, is the fifth-longest cave in Türkiye.
en.Q31189264: Kaşgari Murtaza Efendi Mosque is an 18th-century mosque in Eyüpsultan. It is called Murteza Efendi Mosque after its founder and Kaşgari Mosque because the first sheikh of the lodge that once stood here came from Kashgar. It lies between İdrisköşkü Street, which leads from Eyüp Sultan to the Pierre Loti café, and Hüsamefendi Street, with courtyard gates opening onto both.
en.Q31189278: Saçlı Abdülkadir Efendi Mosque is a 16th-century mosque close to the square of Eyüp Sultan Mosque in Istanbul. It has a single dome and stands on a raised lower storey, partly reflecting classical Ottoman architecture. The original mosque, built in 1538 over his father's tomb, is the now-roofless section adjoining it on the right.
en.Q31189359: Kuzuyayla Nature Park is in the Kartepe district of Kocaeli. Declared a park in 2011, it has rich vegetation and views of Lake Sapanca.
en.Q31189480: Kiremitçi Süleyman Çelebi Mosque, also known as the Red Mosque (Kızıl Cami), is a historic mosque in Eyüpsultan built in 1531 by Kiremitçi Süleyman Çelebi. It stands at the corner of Zalpaşa Street and Kızıldeğirmeni Street, opposite a fountain built by Sokollu Mehmed Pasha, next to which is the Afife Hatun Lodge.
en.Q31189535: The Tomb of İzzet Efendi, Minister of Post and Telegraph, is on Sultan Reşat Street in Eyüpsultan, opposite the Grand Vizier Hüsrev Pasha Lodge and to the right of the tomb of Navy Minister Bozcaadalı Hasan Hüsnü Pasha. The open-roofed tomb has a marble front, and the 'Bismillahirrahmanirrahim' above its door is in celî sülüs script. It is dated 1891.
en.Q31189554: Günpınar (Gürpınar) Waterfall is on the Şuhul stream, a tributary of the Tohma, in the Darende district of Malatya.
en.Q31189561: The Great Offensive Martyrs' Cemetery was built in memory of 275 officers and 2,150 soldiers who fell during the Great Offensive, the Turkish army's attack on Greek forces in the Turkish War of Independence.
en.Q31189944: Bülbül Mescidi is a small mosque in the Mecidiye quarter of central Kütahya, thought to date from the early 19th century. Its builder and date are uncertain, but court records list it as the Yakup Çavuş Mescidi, so it existed before 1830 and is said to have been built by Yakup Çavuş.
en.Q31190010: Kop Mountain is part of the Eastern Black Sea Mountains, south of Bayburt, between the valleys of the Çoruh and Karasu rivers. At 2,918 m it carries an important route from the Black Sea region to Eastern Anatolia and lies within the Kop Mountain Defence Historical National Park.
en.Q31190277: Çatak Canyon is a canyon in the Azdavay district of Kastamonu.
en.Q31190553: The Exchange House (Mübadele Evi) is a museum opened in 2016 in the Görükle quarter of Nilüfer, Bursa.
en.Q31190593: Silahi (Selahi) Mehmed Bey Mosque is on Zalpaşa Street in Eyüpsultan, opposite Zal Mahmud Pasha Mosque (1551). Its founder, Silahşor Mehmet Bey, is buried beside it. It is also known as Bey Mosque, Sürahi Mescidi and Silahşor Mehmet Bey Mescidi.
en.Q31190761: Homer Valley is a 7 km recreation area in the Bornova district of İzmir, opened by İzmir Metropolitan Municipality in May 2008 and extended in 2010. Homer is thought to have lived in a cave in the valley.
en.Q31190849: Muradiye Waterfall, 8 km north of Muradiye in Van province, is named after Sultan Murad IV, who passed this way on his Baghdad campaign. It is 18 m high and admired for both its beauty and its surrounding vegetation. The Bendimahi stream, formed by waters gathering on the Çaldıran plain, flows through the narrow, deep Gönderme Gorge, cut in young volcanic rock, to reach the Muradiye plain.
en.Q31190853: Tomara Waterfall is in the Şiran district of Gümüşhane, in the valley of the Tomara stream, a tributary of the Kelkit. It is named after the tomara plant that grows nearby.
en.Q31192398: Zeynel Bey Tomb is a historic tomb in Hasankeyf, Batman. The Aq Qoyunlu ruler Uzun Hasan built it for his son Zeynel Bey, who died at the Battle of Otlukbeli in 1473.
en.Q31193111: The Atatürk House Museum in Kayseri opened in 1983 and displays belongings of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.
en.Q31193276: Akgöl (Bayındır Lake) is a karst lake in the Yeşilova district of Burdur, between Acıgöl and Lake Salda. Around it lie the villages of Aşağıkırlı, Yukarıkırlı, Dereköy, Orhanlı, Taşpınar and Bayındır. It is also called Bayındır Lake after the nearby village, and Çorak Göl. The lake formed inside a polje.
en.Q31193307: Cezeri Kasım Pasha Mosque on Zalpaşa Street in Eyüpsultan was built in 1515 by Cezerizade Nişancı Kasım Pasha, who also built mosques in Cağaloğlu (Istanbul) and Thessaloniki. It is built of cut stone with brick courses, has a single dome and a three-domed portico in front.
en.Q31193398: The Ankara Palas Hotel is a historic building on İstasyon Boulevard in Nazilli, Aydın, built as a hotel in 1923–1930.
en.Q31355448: Zegani Church, also called Zaki Church, is a medieval Georgian church within the village of Dirsekkaya in the Çıldır district of Ardahan, in the historic Javakheti region. Both its names come from the vanished village of Zaki or Zegani.
en.Q31454590: The Nemrut Caldera is the caldera of Mount Nemrut in Bitlis Province.
en.Q31503259: Raman Mountain is a mountain in the east of Türkiye's Southeastern Anatolia Region.
en.Q31510998: Mount Spil is 24 km from Manisa city along the southern road and about 50 km from İzmir along the northern road.
en.Q31511896: Kurtik Mountain, one of the main peaks around Muş, rises to 2,645 metres south-west of the town and runs north-west to south-east.
en.Q31524766: Ekecik Mountain is in the central district of Aksaray, in Central Anatolia. It is 2,133 metres high and has two summits from east to west. The eastern summit is open to the public; a military radar base stands on the western one.
en.Q31529089: Bulkaz Mountain is the second-highest mountain in Uşak province. With Murat Mountain and Ahır Mountain it forms the province's natural northern, north-eastern and eastern boundary with Afyonkarahisar.
en.Q31530091: Beydağı is a 2,800-metre mountain in the Zara district of Sivas, 70 km from Sivas. It is the province's second-highest mountain after Kösedağ (2,815 m) near Suşehri.
en.Q31564556: Keltepe is a hill in the Beypazarı district of Ankara.
en.Q31571918: Akdağ is a 2,466-metre mountain of the Yalnızçam range in the Olur district of Erzurum. It runs roughly east–west south of Olur town; part of it lies in the Oltu district.
en.Q31790695: Anıt Park is a park in the Yenişehir district of Diyarbakır.
en.Q34894335: Keban Dam Lake lies between Elazığ, Tunceli and Erzincan provinces and was formed by the Keban Dam on the Euphrates. With an area of 675 km², it is Türkiye's fourth-largest lake and second-largest reservoir, holding 30.1 billion m³ of water.
en.Q34907104: Lake Menzelet is a reservoir in Kahramanmaraş.
en.Q34929634: Tahtalı Pond in the Tahtalı quarter of Derince, Kocaeli, is one of the largest ponds (small reservoirs) in Türkiye.
en.Q3555814: The Ayvalık Islands are a group of islands, large and small, in the Ayvalık district of Balıkesir. The largest is Alibey (Cunda) Island, which is now joined by a bridge to Lale Island and by a causeway to Ayvalık, so it is now effectively a peninsula.
en.Q35704578: Gölhisar Lake is a karst lake in the Gölhisar district of Burdur. It was once also called Yamadı Lake and Uylupınar Lake after nearby villages.
en.Q3696280: Değirmendere is a neighbourhood of Gölcük, Kocaeli. Formerly a town with its own municipality, it was merged into Gölcük in 2008.
en.Q4063050: Düdensuyu Cave (Altınbeşik Cave) is a cave in the İbradı district of Antalya.
en.Q416948: Akdağ is a mountain in Denizli and Afyonkarahisar provinces, between Çivril, Kızılören and Sandıklı. Its two summits rise to 2,446 and 2,345 metres. It is the second-highest mountain in the Aegean Region.
en.Q4200748: İnceburun is the northernmost point of Anatolia, at the north-west tip of the Sinop Peninsula, 20 km from Sinop.
en.Q4232172: Kopmuş Burnu is a cape on Türkiye's Black Sea coast at Esenkıyı beach, in the Hopa district of Artvin. Its Laz name is Kotmishi or Kotmisha; Kiepert's 1854 map calls it "Kopmysch Burun".
en.Q4306139: The Kaleiçi Museum is a private museum in two buildings in Kaleiçi, Antalya, both registered as protected cultural heritage. One is an Orthodox church, the other a traditional Turkish house.
en.Q4499143: Alaeddin Hill is a hill in the centre of Konya with important historic buildings, including the Alaeddin Mosque, whose courtyard holds the graves of eight Anatolian Seljuk sultans.
en.Q4505024: The Church of Surp Krikor Lusavoriç is an Armenian Apostolic church in Kayseri, first built in the 12th century.
en.Q462630: The ancient city of Tralles lies north of Aydın on a wide, high plateau on the southern slope of Kestane Mountain (Mesogis). Because ancient texts took the Maeander river or Mount Mesogis as the border, the city is sometimes placed in Caria and sometimes in Lydia.
en.Q47463359: Eğirdir Han is a caravanserai on the lake shore 3 km south of Eğirdir, Isparta, on the Eğirdir–Konya route. It was built in 1237 under Kaykhusraw II. Its inscription is dated AH 635 (1237/38), so construction is thought to have begun under Sultan Alaeddin Keykubad I and been finished by his son after his sudden death.
en.Q47484780: İpek Han is a two-storey inn in the Hanlar district of Bursa, built in the 15th century by the Ottoman sultan Mehmed I to provide income for the Green Complex.
en.Q49105436: Atatürk Republic Tower is a tower in Ankara, built by Keçiören Municipality and opened on 18 March 2024.
en.Q49175319: The Çağrankaya Highlands are three summer pastures (Aşağı Yayla, Kurtlar Yaylası and Büyük Yayla) at 2,300 metres, 9 km north-west of İkizdere, Rize. Their terrain suits off-roading, winter sports, trekking and highland tourism, and campers and nature lovers flock here in summer.
en.Q49321623: Cleopatra Beach is a Blue Flag beach in the Alanya district of Antalya. It is named after Cleopatra: the Roman general Mark Antony is said to have given Alanya to her, and she is said to have swum here whenever she was in the area.
en.Q49371580: Yuvacık is an area of the Başiskele district of Kocaeli.
en.Q49640199: Halilbey Island is the largest of the seven islands in Lake Uluabat, Bursa. It belongs to the village of Eskikaraağaç in Karacabey.
en.Q4992344: Shatberdi Monastery is a medieval Georgian monastery in the village of Okumuşlar, formerly Boselta, in the central district of Artvin, in the historic Klarjeti region.
en.Q50669047: Ali Pasha Bazaar is an Ottoman-era covered bazaar in Edirne.
en.Q527767: Bursa Botanical Park is a 400-decare park on the İzmir–İstanbul road, next to Bursa Zoo. Opened in 1998, it is a first-degree protected site. It is run by Burfaş and entry is free.
en.Q52790862: Gazi Süleyman Pasha Mosque, or Little Hagia Sophia, is a mosque in the Vize district of Kırklareli. It was built in the 6th century, under Emperor Justinian I, as a basilica-style church and is thought to have been converted into a mosque in the 15th century, after Vize came firmly under Ottoman rule. Its structure is compared to Hagia Sophia and Hagia Irene.
en.Q53844808: The Historic Gasworks (Tarihî Havagazı Fabrikası) is a former gas factory in İzmir that now hosts cultural and arts events.
en.Q54915757: Balibey Han is a three-storey inn built in Bursa in the late 15th century to lodge caravans coming from outside the city to buy from or sell to the shops of the Grand Bazaar.
en.Q54935354: Taşhan (Voyvoda Han) is a 17th-century Ottoman building on Gaziosmanpaşa Boulevard in the historic centre of Tokat.
en.Q55030033: Germuş Church, or the Church of Surp Asdvadzadzin, is an Armenian church in the Germuş (Dağeteği) quarter of Haliliye, Şanlıurfa. It was restored in 1881 by Hagop Ardvisyan.
en.Q55524133: The Tanır Inscription is a Hittite-era rock inscription in Luwian at Yukarı Boğaz near the town of Tanır, Afşin (Kahramanmaraş), heavily worn by the elements. It is carved on a smoothed rock face about 2.7 metres above the ground. The name of the city of Malatya can be read in the middle; six illegible hieroglyphs on the right may name one of its rulers.
en.Q56244780: Fethiye Mosque in the Yeni Mahalle quarter of central Kars is a former church converted into a mosque. Built at the end of the 19th century, it was known as the Alexander Nevsky Church or the Cossack Church.
en.Q56260284: The Emine Göğüş Cuisine Museum introduces Gaziantep's food culture through photographs of local dishes and kitchen tools used in the past.
en.Q56279770: The Battle of Manzikert Historical National Park is in the Malazgirt district of Muş.
en.Q56435475: Çubuk City Museum is a museum in the Çubuk district of Ankara. It was created by restoring the Bekir Ağalar Mansion, one of the few historic buildings in the district, which belonged to a wealthy family of its time. It opened as an exhibition hall in 2015 and was registered as a city museum by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism in 2017.
en.Q56438546: The Satıkadın Museum is a museum in the Kahramankazan district of Ankara, opened in 2014. It is the restored house of Satı Çırpan, one of the Republic's first women members of parliament. It displays her belongings and clothes along with many historic photographs and paintings.
en.Q56438674: The TCDD Malıköy Railway Station Museum is in the Polatlı district of Ankara. During the Battle of Sakarya, Malıköy, a village and railway station near Polatlı, was the most important base after the main command centre. The Turkish army used it as a supply centre, infirmary, ammunition depot and airstrip.
en.Q56439966: Bafra Archaeology and Ethnography Museum is a museum in the Bafra district of Samsun.
en.Q56439995: The Ankara University Faculty of Agriculture Museum is in the Altındağ district of Ankara. A commission set up in 2005 decided to open it, and it opened in 2007. It has two halls on the ground floor and 10 rooms and a corridor upstairs.
en.Q56440031: The Gendarmerie Museum is a museum in Ahlatlıbel, Ankara. The idea came up in 1995 and work began in 1996. It opened on 21 November 2005 to present the history of the gendarmerie and pass this military heritage on to future generations.
en.Q56440080: The Living Museum is a folk museum in the Beypazarı district of Ankara, founded in 2007 by a civic initiative.
en.Q56479480: The Ankara Atatürk House Museum is a copy of the house in Thessaloniki where Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, founder of the Republic of Türkiye, was born. It was built on the grounds of the Atatürk Forest Farm to mark Atatürk's 100th birthday, following a decision of the Ankara Chamber of Commerce board on 6 November 1980.
en.Q56479502: Yalvaç Museum displays archaeological finds in the Yalvaç district of Isparta. Construction began in 1963 and was completed in 1965; the museum opened to the public on 9 September 1966.
en.Q59260319: Öresin Han, also called Tepesi Delik Han, is a caravanserai on the Silk Road between Aksaray and Nevşehir, about 24 km from Aksaray.
en.Q5991880: Etz Hayim Synagogue is one of the historic synagogues of Kemeraltı in İzmir.
en.Q5994759: The Nevvar Salih İşgören Great Mosque in İzmir was built by the Nevvar Salih İşgören Foundation and was planned as the largest mosque in the Aegean region.
en.Q5994824: Susuzdede Park is a 46,000 m² park on the hill of the same name in the Göztepe quarter of Konak, İzmir. Before the Republic the hill was called Aya Agapi; it took the name of a holy man known as Susuz Dede after he died and was buried here.
en.Q5994960: Aşık Veysel Recreation Area is a 231,000 m² park in the Bornova district of İzmir, named after the folk poet Âşık Veysel. Work began in 2008 and it was opened by İzmir Metropolitan Municipality on 25 September 2010.
en.Q5995062: The Church of the Archangels, locally known as Kumyaka Church, is a Byzantine church in Kumyaka, Mudanya, Bursa, thought to date from 780. It was completed between 780 and 797 under the Byzantine emperor Constantine. Much repaired, it has a square plan and a dome.
en.Q5995516: The Latife Hanım Mansion Memorial House is a museum on Bahriye Üçok Boulevard in Karşıyaka, İzmir.
en.Q5995605: Uşakizade Mansion is a mansion in İzmir.
en.Q5996572: Selime Cathedral is in the village of Selime, in the Güzelyurt district of Aksaray.
en.Q5996935: The Maidens' Monument (Bakireler Anıtı) stands in the sea 50 metres off Süreyya Beach in Küçükyalı, Maltepe (Istanbul). Designed by the architect Münci Tangör at the request of Süreyya İlmen, it was begun in 1939 but, because of the Second World War, only finished in 1946.
en.Q5997427: Baltalı Kapı was the entrance gate of ancient Mylasa and is today the northern gate of Milas. It stands west of Esentepe in the Hacıapdi quarter, measures 5 x 12 metres and was built at the end of the 1st century BC. It is named after the double-headed axe, known in antiquity as the labrys, carved on its keystone.
en.Q5998091: Santissimo Rosario is a Catholic church in İzmir.
en.Q5998305: The Portuguese Synagogue is one of the historic synagogues of Kemeraltı in İzmir; the building is now used for cultural events.
en.Q6000139: Sümbüllü Church is in the Ihlara Valley in Aksaray.
en.Q6000577: Yeşil Ada (Green Island) is one of two islands at Eğirdir on Lake Eğirdir, the other being Can Ada. Besides its natural beauty it has historic sights such as the Church of St Stephen, along with fish restaurants and family guesthouses.
en.Q6000752: Lake Zinav (Sinan Lake) is a landslide-dammed lake in the Reşadiye district of Tokat. It is 1 km long, 70–500 m wide, up to 15 m deep and covers 26 hectares.
en.Q6001249: Taşköprü is a seven-arched, 68-metre bridge over the Gökırmak river in the Taşköprü district of Kastamonu, built in the time of the Çobanoğulları principality.
en.Q6003007: İvaz Pasha Mosque is a mosque in the city of Manisa.
en.Q6003585: Tarsus Clock Tower stands at the north-east corner of the Great Mosque in Tarsus, Mersin. Encouraged by District Governor Ziya Bey, Feyzullah Ağa (Aykut), a notable of Frengülüs (Çiçekli) village, had it built in 1894 at a cost of 25,000 kuruş and brought a large clock from Europe.
en.Q6004186: The Tomb of Sultan Reşad in the Eyüpsultan district of Istanbul is the burial place of Mehmed V Reşad, the 35th Ottoman sultan. Designed by the architect Kemaleddin Bey in the national architectural style and built in 1911–1912, it is octagonal, of cut stone and marble, with a high lead-covered dome.
en.Q6004947: Yozgat Clock Tower stands on Yozgat's main square. It has a single balcony and was built in 1908 by the mayor of the time, Tevfikizade Ahmet Bey.
en.Q6004956: Irmak Bath, built in Adana in 1494 by the Ramadanid Beylik, is one of the city's oldest bathhouses. It stands on the remains of an old Roman building.
en.Q6005220: Ali Vafi Mansion, also known as Ayvazpaşazade or Memduh Pasha Mansion, first belonged to an Armenian banker; in 1915 Ali Vafi of Crete bought it. It is said to have once had a mint and a water-powered lift in its garden. It is still rented and in use, with Ali Vafi Grove behind it.
en.Q6005543: Hekimbaşı Mansion is a waterside mansion at Anadoluhisarı in the Beykoz district of Istanbul. It is thought to have been built in 1697 by Amcazade Hüseyin Pasha. It is named after Chief Physician Salih Efendi, of the Abdulmejid I era, who bought and enlarged it in the 1850s.
en.Q6005606: Commodore Remzi Bey Mansion is a historic waterside mansion in the Anadoluhisarı quarter of Beykoz, Istanbul. Built in 1917, it was sold to General Mümtaz Aktay Pasha and bought in 1972 by Erdal İnönü.
en.Q6005866: Bayaz Han (White Inn) is a historic inn in Gaziantep built in 1909 by Bayaz Ahmet Efendi. After the First World War it also served as a military headquarters and a prison. Restored in 2009, it is now a museum of Gaziantep crafts such as copperwork and kutnu fabric, with cafés and restaurants inside.
en.Q6006036: Firuzbey Mosque is a 14th-century mosque in the Milas district of Muğla.
en.Q6006443: Naib Bath is a historic hamam just south of Gaziantep Castle. Built in 1640, it was restored in 2009 under the award-winning Culture Route Project.
en.Q6006724: Algazi Synagogue is one of the historic synagogues of Kemeraltı in İzmir and, after Bet Israel, the largest synagogue in the city.
en.Q6007001: Kara Mustafa Pasha Caravanserai, also called Silahtar Mustafa Pasha Caravanserai, was built in 1660 as part of a complex by the Ottoman vizier Merzifonlu Silahtar Mustafa Pasha. It is in the İncesu district of Kayseri.
en.Q6007327: The Coppersmiths' Bazaar (Bakırcılar Çarşısı) is a historic bazaar in Gaziantep, named after the copperware sold there.
en.Q6007392: Hamamönü is a historic quarter in the Altındağ district of Ankara and one of the city's oldest settlements.
en.Q6007692: Alay Han is a 13th-century caravanserai from the Anatolian Seljuk period.
en.Q6007763: Kızıl Medrese (the Red Madrasa) is a historic building in the Dağkapı quarter of central Cizre, Şırnak.
en.Q6008102: Sarpıncık Lighthouse is a lighthouse in the Karaburun district of İzmir.
en.Q6009091: Gazi Süleyman Pasha Mosque is a historic mosque in Göynük, Bolu, built between 1331 and 1335 by Gazi Süleyman Pasha, son of Orhan Gazi, with a single minaret and a single wooden dome. It stands in the centre of Göynük, opposite the Müderrisoğlu Mansion, with the Tomb of Akşemsettin beside it.
en.Q6009237: Pürenli Seki Church is in the Ihlara Valley in Aksaray. It is carved into the rock in four sections. Its frescoes date from the early 10th to the 12th century, and there are graves in the narthex floor. Its scenes from the childhood of Jesus and the Gospels, such as the prophets' prophecy, Mary with bishops, the Annunciation, the Visitation and the adoration of the shepherds, are important.
en.Q6009286: The Abdulaziz Hunting Lodge, or Kasr-ı Hümayun, is a baroque and Empire-style pavilion in İzmit. It took its final form under Sultan Abdulaziz and is known as the only small palace the Ottomans built outside Istanbul. Designed by Garabet Amira Balyan, it is now a museum.
en.Q6010193: Kayseri Cumhuriyet Square is a square in the Melikgazi district of Kayseri.
en.Q6010375: Tophane Marshal Zeki Pasha Mansion is a Bosphorus waterside mansion built in the early 20th century by the Levantine architect Alexandre Vallaury for Mustafa Zeki Pasha, Marshal of the Imperial Arsenal and one of Abdulhamid II's commanders.
en.Q6011467: Spil Mountain National Park lies within Manisa and İzmir provinces. Covering Mount Spil and its surroundings, it was declared on 22 April 1968 and includes the Atalanı area near the summit.
en.Q6011581: Hasip Pasha Mansion was built in the second half of the 19th century in neoclassical/neo-baroque style and carries nearly 150 years of memories of a family known in Turkish science and art. It has a stone service floor and two timber-framed floors; each floor has two staircases, two large halls, a main salon and six rooms.
en.Q6012667: Zarif Mustafa Pasha Mansion is a waterside mansion in the Beykoz district of Istanbul. Mustafa Pasha bought it in 1848, and it has stayed in the same family ever since. Once among the largest buildings on the Bosphorus, only its selamlık survives. It was damaged when a cargo ship hit it in 1990, and later restored.
en.Q6012705: Pirinç Han is an inn in Bursa built by Sultan Bayezid II.
en.Q6013142: The Republic Tree (Cumhuriyet Ağacı) is a monument in Gündoğdu Square, Konak, İzmir.
en.Q6013357: Düldül Mountain, north-east of the Düziçi district of Osmaniye, is the highest peak of the Amanos (Nur) Mountains at 2,448 metres. It has three high summits: Gökçe and Kefen in Osmaniye, and Kaya Düldül (Eğri), 2,110 m, near the Berke Dam on the Kahramanmaraş side.
en.Q6013457: Şahinbey War Museum in Gaziantep tells the story of the Defence of Antep. It displays weapons, objects, clothing, books and magazines from the war; part of the museum is in a cave that served as an important shelter during the fighting.
en.Q6013556: Şarapsa Han is a 13th-century building on the banks of the Serapsu stream, by the highway 15 km west of Alanya.
en.Q6013803: Mount Kato, or the Kato Mountains, is a mountain range in the Beytüşşebap district of Şırnak, also known as the mountains Alexander the Great could not cross.
en.Q6013884: Kordon (Birinci Kordon or Kordonboyu) is the avenue, waterfront and public promenade along the southern shore of the Gulf of İzmir. In the Konak district, it runs between Cumhuriyet Square and Alsancak Port, with landscaped green areas, walking and cycling paths, squares and the Alsancak ferry pier between Atatürk Avenue and the sea.
en.Q6014179: Lake Hafik, also called Büyük Göl or Koçhisar Lake, is a small karst lake north of the Hafik district of Sivas. It is 1,100 m long and 1,000 m wide, lies at 1,295 m, covers about 80 hectares and is 2–6 m deep.
en.Q6015778: Buca Yedigöller is a 100,000 m² park in the Buca district of İzmir, founded in December 2003 on the model of Yedigöller National Park in Bolu. It originally had seven ponds linked by waterfalls; a 2022 redesign reduced them to three.
en.Q6016284: Alifuatpaşa Bridge, or the Bayezid II Bridge, is a bridge in the town of Alifuatpaşa, Geyve (Sakarya), built by Sultan Bayezid II.
en.Q6016566: Hatuniye Mosque was built in Amasya in 1510 by Bülbül Hatun, wife of Sultan Bayezid II and mother of Prince Ahmet.
en.Q6016858: St Peter's Church (Aziz Bedros) is a historic Armenian church in Gaziantep, built in 1723 according to available sources. It came to light in 2005 during municipal road works and has since been turned into a museum, the Ömer Ersoy Culture Centre.
en.Q6018307: Taşhoron Church (Stone Church / Üç Horan), or the Church of the Holy Trinity, is in the Çavuşoğlu quarter of Yeşilyurt, Malatya. It was built in the second half of the 18th century by Armenians or Syriacs.
en.Q6018353: Eskişehir Mevlevi Lodge is a former Mevlevi lodge within the Kurşunlu Complex in the Paşa quarter of Odunpazarı, Eskişehir.
en.Q6018846: Gito (Kito) is a highland pasture at 2,070 metres in the Çat valley of Çamlıhemşin, Rize, 31 km from the district centre.
en.Q6018889: Tunalı Hilmi Street is a street in the Kavaklıdere area of Çankaya, Ankara.
en.Q6019451: Atça Park lies where eight main streets meet in Atça and is the centre of the neighbourhood.
en.Q6019534: Zühtü Pasha Mosque was built in 1883 by Ahmed Zühdü Pasha, Minister of Education under Sultan Abdulhamid II. It stands in Zühtüpaşa (Kadıköy) and has masonry walls and a wooden dome.
en.Q6019583: The Church of Our Lady of Częstochowa is a historic church in Polonezköy, in the Beykoz district of Istanbul.
en.Q6019963: Kent Park is a park of about 270,000 m² in Eskişehir, stretching along the Porsuk river between the bus station and the Gökmeydan quarter.
en.Q6019974: Mehmet Çavuş Mosque is a mosque in İçerenköy, Istanbul. Built in 1665, it was rebuilt in 1924 and renamed İçerenköy Mosque.
en.Q6020259: Sadullah Pasha Mansion is a waterside mansion on the Bosphorus in Çengelköy, Üsküdar. It is one of the classic Ottoman-era wooden yalıs of the strait.
en.Q6020580: Akhan Caravanserai is in the Akhan quarter of Pamukkale, Denizli, at kilometre 7 of the Denizli–Afyonkarahisar–Ankara road. The covered hall was completed in 1253 and the courtyard in 1254; it was commissioned by Governor Seyfettin Karasungur bin Abdullah.
en.Q6020905: The Monastery of St Nicholas (Aya Nikola) in Kıyıköy, Vize (Kırklareli), is one of the oldest rock-cut monasteries in the world.
en.Q6021763: The Hüdavendigar Complex is a group of buildings in Bursa built by Murad I, the third Ottoman sultan.
en.Q6021890: Döner Kümbet was built in Kayseri in 1276 for Şah Cihan Hatun, daughter of the Seljuk sultan Alaeddin Keykubad I, and is also known as the Şah Cihan Hatun Tomb. It stands on the Talas road.
en.Q6022256: Kütahya Castle is a castle from the Byzantine period in the city of Kütahya.
en.Q6022313: Kesik Köprü, formerly Gürcü Hüseyin Bridge, is a Seljuk bridge built in 1213 over the Kızılırmak near Sivas, on the old Kayseri road.
en.Q6022474: Talazan Bridge crosses the Kelkit river 15 km from Niksar, Tokat. Talazan means 'sturdy, reliable'.
en.Q6023590: Dipsiz Göl ('Bottomless Lake') is a lake in the Doğanşar district of Sivas, right beside the Doğanşar–Sivas road near Çatpınar village, 16 km from Doğanşar and 82 km from Sivas. It was formed when the ground over a spring collapsed, and is named for its unknown depth; amateur measurements put it at 14 metres.
en.Q6023683: Harput Great Mosque was built in 1156–1157 by the Artuqid ruler Fahrettin Karaaslan in Harput, in today's Elazığ province. It is considered one of the oldest mosques in Anatolia.
en.Q6023921: Pokut Plateau is a highland pasture at 2,032 metres south of Çamlıhemşin, Rize, between the valleys of the Fırtına and Hala streams.
