en.Q6024089: Kargı Han lies west of Alanya, north of the Kargı stream, in the village of Beydiğin within Manavgat.
en.Q6024218: The Suleiman the Magnificent Fountain is a historic three-sided stone fountain in classical style in the Büyükçekmece district of Istanbul. Mimar Sinan built it in 1566, together with Kurşunlu Han and the Suleiman the Magnificent Bridge, as Suleiman set out on the Szigetvár campaign. It still supplies drinking water.
en.Q6024263: Karatay Han is a caravanserai built by Celaleddin Karatay on the Kayseri–Malatya road.
en.Q6025093: İmaret Mosque is the only Ottoman mosque in Akşehir. It was built by Hasan Pasha in 1510.
en.Q6025611: Trabzon Atatürk Pavilion stands in a small pine grove in the Soğuksu area of Ortahisar, Trabzon.
en.Q6026104: Mençuna Waterfall is a waterfall in the Arhavi district of Artvin.
en.Q6026122: Şahadet Mosque, also called Kale Mosque or Saray Mosque, is a historic mosque in the Tophane area of Bursa.
en.Q6026552: Ferhad Pasha Mosque is a mosque in Çatalca, Istanbul.
en.Q6026745: Hacı Ziya Bey Mosque is a small mosque in the Yeni Camii quarter of Söke, Aydın, built in 1894 by Hacı Ziya Bey, a local notable. It is a square, single-domed building about 10 m on each side. Vaults carry the dome, and each wall rises in the middle into a large arch topped by a triangular pediment.
en.Q6026923: This church, also known as the Kızlar Monastery, is carved into steep rocks about 3 km from the centre of Güzelyurt.
en.Q6027466: The Myndos Gate is a historic site west of central Bodrum and an important point of the city walls of Halicarnassus. Because the western walls crossed the plain, they were strengthened with towers of about 7 x 8.5 metres; one of the gate's two towers survives almost to its original height.
en.Q6027628: The Tomb of Sheikh Edebali holds the remains of Sheikh Edebali, father-in-law and teacher of Osman Gazi, founder of the Ottoman state. It is in the Cumhuriyet quarter of Bilecik.
en.Q6027830: Kirazlı Monastery is a complex of a monastery, a church and other buildings at the foot of the mountain known in antiquity as Didumus. Its masonry shows it was a 19th-century religious building used by the Greek Orthodox community. Its foundations and wall remains show it had two floors over a basement.
en.Q6027918: Ballıkayalar is a rocky canyon valley near the village of Tavşanlı in Gebze, Kocaeli, protected as a nature park.
en.Q6027957: Bayezid Pasha Mosque was built in Amasya in 1414 by the regional governor Bayezid Pasha.
en.Q6028140: Nuri Pasha Mansion is a Bosphorus waterside mansion on the shore of Kanlıca, Beykoz.
en.Q6028239: İznik Castle dates from the Roman period and stands near İznik Lake. Its construction began in 310 under Antigonus, son of Philip. In 330 the castle held off enemy attacks. It was heavily repaired in the Byzantine period, when its circuit grew from about 3,000 to about 4,500 metres. The walls are about 10–13 metres high.
en.Q6029742: Siyavuşpaşa Pavilion, also called Havuzlu Köşk (Çavuş Başı), is a pavilion in the Bahçelievler district of Istanbul. Its exact date is unknown, but it is thought to have been built in 1571–72.
en.Q6029758: Orhan Gazi Mosque is a mosque in Bilecik built by Bayezid I.
en.Q6029950: Şehzade Burhaneddin Efendi Mansion is a wooden Bosphorus waterside mansion, partly neo-baroque, on the shore of Yeniköy, Sarıyer. With 64 rooms, it is among the largest on the Bosphorus. It took its name after Prince Burhaneddin, son of Abdulhamid II, bought it in 1911; when the Egyptian Ahmet İhsan Bey later bought it, it also became known as the Egyptians' Mansion.
en.Q6030271: Dumlu Castle stands on a hard limestone hill about 75 m high, 17 km northwest of Ceyhan, west of the Dumlu (Tumlu) quarter of Sağkaya. It is thought to date from the 12th century. Its walls run 800 metres and have eight towers. A watchtower stands at the eastern corner facing the plain, and its only gate faces east. Inside are building remains and cisterns.
en.Q6030600: Sadabad Mosque, also called Kağıthane Mosque, is a mosque on the bank of the Kağıthane stream in Istanbul.
en.Q6030722: Çeşnigir Mosque in Manisa was built in 1474 by Çeşnigir Sinan Bey, a freed slave of Mehmed II, and is one of the city's oldest mosques. It once also had a library.
en.Q6031100: The Independence Road (İstiklal Yolu) is the 344 km route from the coast at İnebolu through Kastamonu and Çankırı to Ankara. During the War of Independence, ammunition landed at İnebolu was carried along it to the front by ox carts. In 2018 an area of 2,357 decares was declared a national park.
en.Q6031340: Şah Sultan Mosque is on Silahtar Ağa Street in central Eyüpsultan, Istanbul; the mosque and its surroundings were once a Sünbüli dervish lodge. It was commissioned from Mimar Sinan in 1533 by Şah Sultan, daughter of Sultan Selim I. Sheikh Merkezzade Ahmet Efendi is buried in its tomb.
en.Q6031765: Ahmed Fethi Pasha Mansion is a wooden Bosphorus waterside mansion in traditional Ottoman style on the shore of Kuzguncuk, Üsküdar.
en.Q6032179: Samsun National Garden is a city park in the Canik district of Samsun.
en.Q6032665: Hatay Castle, or Antakya Castle, is in the Antakya district of Hatay. After Istanbul's, its walls are the longest city walls in Türkiye. They were built around 300 BC under Seleucus I Nicator, one of Alexander the Great's generals, and extended in Roman and Byzantine times to a length of 23,600 metres.
en.Q6032732: Kaptanpaşa Mosque is a historic two-storey, square-plan mosque of cut stone on Eyüpsultan İskele Street, Istanbul.
en.Q6032910: İshak Fakih Mosque in Kütahya, dated 1433, is a late Germiyanid work built by İshak Fakih, a noted local scholar of Islamic law. It has cut-stone and brick walls and a showy façade; its three-part porch has cut stones framed with red brick, and one section of it serves as a tomb.
en.Q6032977: Side Museum is a museum within the ancient city of Side.
en.Q6033431: Anzer Plateau lies 35 km south-west of İkizdere and 54 km from Rize. It is divided into Lower Anzer (Çiçekliköy) and Upper Anzer (Ballıköy). Famous for its honey, it is also an important ecotourism area.
en.Q6033460: Mount Verçenik (Üçdoruk) is a 3,711-metre peak of the Kaçkar Mountains in the eastern Black Sea section of the North Anatolian Mountains. It is the second-highest summit of the Eastern Black Sea Mountains after Kaçkar and the eighth-highest mountain in Türkiye.
en.Q6033666: Karesi Tomb in Balıkesir was built for Karesi Bey, founder of the Karesi Beylik. Destroyed in the 1898 Balıkesir earthquake, it was rebuilt by the mayor of the time, Hayrettin Bey. Karesi Bey and his five sons are buried here.
en.Q6033748: Halaskargazi Street runs about 1.3 km from the Harbiye junction to Şişli Mosque in Istanbul. It is lined with office buildings, banks, shopping arcades, museums and restaurants; the Kenter Theatre is on this street.
en.Q6033830: Akşebe Sultan Mescidi is a historic small mosque from the Seljuk period in the Alanya district of Antalya.
en.Q6034089: Köprülü Canyon National Park is in the Manavgat district of Antalya. It lies around Köprülü Canyon, 14 km long and 100 m deep, between Bolasan and Beşkonak, with the Köprü river running through it. At 14 km it is Türkiye's longest canyon. The park has cedar forests and rock formations like the fairy chimneys of Cappadocia. The old stone bridge over the Köprü river is still in use.
en.Q6034196: Koçhisar Castle is a castle on a hill just east of Şereflikoçhisar.
en.Q6034420: Botanik Park is a 65,000 m² park in the Çankaya district of Ankara, set up in 1970 between Çankaya Street and Cinnah Street. In the middle are a pool, a children's playground and a flower greenhouse.
en.Q6036038: Timurtaş Pasha Mosque (also called Takkeciler or Takvacılar Mosque) is a mosque near the Small Bedesten in Kütahya.
en.Q6036971: The Kuva-yi Milliye and Republic Monument stands at the southern entrance to Manisa, in the Kayapınar quarter of Yunusemre, west of the D565 road.
en.Q6037156: Hoşkadem Mosque stands in the centre of Kozan, Adana. It is an important building because it dates from the first years after Çukurova came under Turkish rule.
en.Q6037253: Alacalı Mosque stands at the entrance to Kitapçıgil Park in Harput. It is believed to have been built in 1203–1204 under the Artuqids, in the time of Hızır Bey, father of Nureddin Ebü'l-Fazıl Artuk Şah. The small, rectangular mosque probably takes its name ('the multicoloured') from its two-coloured cut stone, a common Artuqid feature.
en.Q6038424: Altınşehir is a neighbourhood in the Başakşehir district of Istanbul and the district's smallest by area.
en.Q6038736: Kokar Church is a 9th-century church in the Ihlara Valley, Aksaray.
en.Q6038772: Çakalburnu Lagoon, or Çakalburnu Fishery, is a lagoon on the south side of the Gulf of İzmir, in the Bahçelerarası quarter of Balçova, west of İnciraltı Urban Forest. It is a first-degree protected site where 121 bird species have been recorded.
en.Q6039025: Ulugöl is a landslide-dammed lake between the villages of Haruniye and Süleymaniye in the Gölköy district of Ordu.
en.Q6039235: Manisa Great Mosque is a mosque in the city of Manisa.
en.Q6040463: Reşat Oyal Culture Park was opened in Bursa in 1955 by Mayor Reşat Oyal under the name Kültürpark.
en.Q6040846: Tütün Hanı (the Tobacco Inn) is an inn in Gaziantep where tobacco merchants once stayed and traded.
en.Q6042955: Samsun Museum, formerly the Samsun Archaeology and Ethnography Museum, displays finds from Samsun and its surroundings from the Chalcolithic, Early Bronze Age, Hittite, Hellenistic, Roman and Ottoman periods.
en.Q6043205: Sülbüs Mountain is a mountain in the Yayladere district of Bingöl.
en.Q6043333: Lake Gaga (Grago) is a landslide lake in the Yassıtaş quarter of Fatsa, Ordu, at kilometre 8 of the Fatsa–Aybastı road.
en.Q6043868: Burmalı Minare Mosque, also called Ulu Mosque or Mahkeme Mosque, is a historic mosque in Amasya. It is named after its spiral minaret and stands out for the Seljuk tomb next to it and its Ottoman-era minaret. It was built in 1237 by Ferruh b. Selçuk, in the reign of the Seljuk sultan Kaykhusraw II.
en.Q6044027: Divlit Volcano is part of the Kula volcanic field, which lies on the Gediz Graben, one of the largest east–west tectonic troughs of the Aegean region. Its unusual landforms were shaped by volcanic activity, tectonic movements, rivers and weather.
en.Q6044488: Ulgar Mountain is a 2,918-metre volcanic mountain between the Posof and Damal districts of Ardahan, where the year's first snow falls. It is covered in snow from November to late April and its summit is almost always in cloud. In summer it is covered with green forests and flowers.
en.Q6044663: Adana Yeni Mosque, also called Antaki Mosque, is a historic mosque in Adana built under the influence of Mamluk architecture.
en.Q6045025: Kırkgöz Bridge stands 7 km from the centre of Bolvadin, Afyonkarahisar. It was built over the Akarçay river in 1150 by the Byzantine emperor Manuel I. Repaired and extended in Seljuk and Ottoman times, it now has 57 arches.
en.Q6045692: Sığacık Castle is in the Seferihisar district of İzmir, in the Sığacık quarter it is named after, just north-east of Sığacık harbour, which is still in use. It is thought to date from the Seljuk period.
en.Q6045732: Bursa Zoo (Soğanlı Zoo) is a zoo built to European standards that opened in Bursa in 1998.
en.Q6046631: Derviş Ağa Mosque is a historic mosque in the Yakutiye district of Erzurum.
en.Q6047039: Cumhuriyet Square is the largest square in Kastamonu and, with Nasrullah Square, one of the city's two main squares. It has been named among the three most beautiful squares in Türkiye.
en.Q6047218: Licese Church is in the Licese hamlet of Asarcık village, Şebinkarahisar (Giresun). It is thought to have been built between 1874 and 1887.
en.Q6047459: Tınaztepe Cave is a large karst cave in Seydişehir, Konya. With a total length of 22 km and a 1,580-metre visitor section, it is one of the longest caves in Türkiye.
en.Q6047922: The Earthquake Culture Museum (Adapazarı Earthquake and Culture Museum) was opened in 2004 by Adapazarı Municipality after four years of construction. It commemorates those who died in the Marmara earthquake of 17 August 1999, tells what happened and raises awareness of earthquakes.
en.Q6048218: Narmanlı Mosque is a historic mosque in the Yakutiye district of Erzurum.
en.Q6048452: Ali Bey Mosque is a mosque in the Ali Bey quarter of central Çankırı. Its inscription shows it was built in 1609.
en.Q6048574: Boyahane Mosque is a historic mosque in the Yakutiye district of Erzurum.
en.Q6048671: The Cevdet Sunay Museum in the Çaykara district of Trabzon is the house where Cevdet Sunay, Türkiye's 5th president, was born and grew up, restored as a museum.
en.Q6048738: Güzelce Aqueduct, also called Gözlüce or Cebeciköy Aqueduct, is a historic aqueduct in the Cebeci quarter of Sultangazi, Istanbul. Built of cut stone, it is 29.5 m high and 155 m long, with 8 arches below and 11 above; its walls are 5.4 m thick at the base and 2.6 m at the top.
en.Q6048854: Ayaz Pasha Mosque is a historic mosque in the central Yakutiye district of Erzurum.
en.Q6048873: Delikliçınar Square, or simply Çınar Square, is one of the main squares of Denizli, in the Merkezefendi district; the metropolitan municipality building stands on it. According to local legend, it is named after a plane tree with a large hole in its trunk that once grew here.
en.Q6049094: Bedrama Castle, or Petroma Castle, is built entirely on natural rock near the Giresun–Gümüşhane road, on the land of Örenkaya and Karaahmetli villages in Tirebolu. It stands on crags east of the Harşit river, overlooking the Harşit valley. Who built it is disputed.
en.Q6049125: Caferiye Mosque is a historic mosque in the Yakutiye district of Erzurum.
en.Q6049420: Yılanlı Church is a church in the Ihlara Valley in Aksaray, dating from the late 9th century.
en.Q6049621: Muğla Kurşunlu Mosque is a 15th-century Ottoman mosque in Muğla.
en.Q6050764: Seyifler Castle is a small Byzantine castle of 80 x 80 m near the village of Seyifler, Ferizli (Sakarya).
en.Q6051024: Kasım Pasha Mosque is a historic mosque in the Yakutiye district of Erzurum.
en.Q6051659: Burma Mosque is in central Uşak. Its construction date is unknown, but the inscription on its door shows it was renovated in 1769.
en.Q6051682: Babaeski Bridge, or Murad IV Bridge, is a historic bridge over the Babaeski stream, a tributary of the Ergene, in the Babaeski district of Kırklareli. It was built in the reign of Murad IV.
en.Q6051748: Harikalar Diyarı (Wonderland) is a park in the Fatih quarter of Sincan, Ankara. Covering 1,320,000 square metres, it is one of Europe's large parks. It opened on 5 October 2004.
en.Q6052467: Bitlis Castle was built in Bitlis in 312 BC by Badlis, one of Alexander the Great's commanders. The city of Bitlis takes its name from him.
en.Q6053222: The Erzincan Plain lies along the Karasu (Euphrates) valley in the Upper Euphrates section of Eastern Anatolia.
en.Q6054013: The İzzet Koyunoğlu City Museum in the Topraklık quarter of Konya was founded by A. R. İzzet Koyunoğlu, from one of Konya's old families, who began collecting in 1913 in an old, typical Konya house. Its holdings include archaeological finds from Konya and its surroundings, books, ethnographic objects and natural history items.
en.Q6054200: Kazdağı National Park is a national park in Edremit, Balıkesir, named after Kazdağı (Mount Ida), which forms the border between the Marmara and Aegean regions.
en.Q6054560: Abdurrahman Ağa Mosque, also called Silahtar Abdurrahman Ağa Mosque or Paşalimanı Mosque, is an Ottoman-era mosque in the Sultantepe quarter of Üsküdar, Istanbul. It was built by Abdurrahman Ağa, sword-bearer of Sultan Mustafa III; work began in 1765 and it opened in 1766.
en.Q6054746: Bakırcı Mosque is a historic mosque in the Yakutiye district of Erzurum.
en.Q6054904: Gürcü Kapı Ali Ağa Mosque is a historic mosque in the Yakutiye district of Erzurum.
en.Q6055439: Tabaklar Mosque, also called Konyalı Biraderler or Debbağlar Mosque, is an Ottoman-era mosque in the Zeynep Kamil quarter of Üsküdar, Istanbul. Built by Hacı Ferhat Ağa and Hacı Mehmet Ağa, it was begun in 1587 and opened in 1588.
en.Q6055656: The Antalya Toy Museum is a toy museum run by Antalya Metropolitan Municipality, opened on 23 April 2011.
en.Q6055841: Alagöz Headquarters Museum: when the enemy advanced as far as Polatlı during the Battle of Sakarya, the Western Front Command chose the village of Alagöz, between Ankara and Polatlı, as its front headquarters. The farmhouse of Türkoğlu Ali Ağa, a villager, served as the headquarters.
en.Q6055954: The Şamil Ekinci Museum is a sports museum in the Ortahisar district of Trabzon. It is open every day except Monday from 09:00 to 18:00.
en.Q6056525: Bilecik Clock Tower is in the garden of Bilecik Town Hall in the city centre.
en.Q6056589: Yumurtatepe is an Early Bronze Age tumulus in the Çamlıca quarter of Yenimahalle, Ankara.
en.Q6056682: The Kossuth House Museum (also called the Hungarian House) is an 18th-century Turkish house in Kütahya, open to visitors since 1982; it belonged to Şeyh Bedreddin Efendi. It displays belongings of the lawyer Lajos Kossuth, a leader of the Hungarian Revolution who lived here in 1850–1851, and objects of Hungarian culture. Kossuth wrote his draft constitution for Hungary in this house.
en.Q6056837: Müderris Abdülbaki Efendi Mosque, or Baki Efendi Mosque, is an Ottoman-era mosque in the Sultantepe quarter of Üsküdar, Istanbul. It was built in 1644 by Abdülbaki Efendi, judge of İzmir and Aleppo, son-in-law of Aziz Mahmud Hüdayi and son of Tiryaki Hasan Pasha.
en.Q6056905: Bürüngüz Mosque is a mosque on Cumhuriyet Square in the Melikgazi district of Kayseri.
en.Q6057486: Karaali Mosque is at Mendepazarı in Uşak. Its date is unknown, and it is said to have been built by a man named Kara Ali. The building bears an inscription dated 1567–1568, but its architecture does not show 16th-century features.
en.Q6057904: Akçakoca Central Mosque in Akçakoca, Düzce, has a roof designed after Seljuk goat-hair tents.
en.Q6058867: Durmuş Yaşar Mansion, formerly the Aliotti Mansion, is a building in the Karşıyaka district of İzmir.
en.Q6059840: Hacı Hesna Hatun Mosque is an Ottoman-era mosque in the Sultantepe quarter of Üsküdar, Istanbul. It was built by Arslan Ağa in the name of his wife Hacı Hesna Hatun, nurse of Mihrimah Sultan; work began in 1584 and it opened in 1585.
en.Q6059842: The Tomb of Yahya Efendi is a masonry tomb by Mimar Sinan, dated 1571, next to the Yahya Efendi Lodge opposite Çırağan Palace in Beşiktaş, Istanbul.
en.Q6060345: Antalya Clock Tower stands at the Kale Kapısı area of Antalya.
en.Q6060451: Hashöyük is a mound in the village of the same name, 35 km from Kırşehir.
en.Q6060632: Süleymaniye Mosque is a mosque in Alanya, Antalya.
en.Q6060925: Kurban Nasuh Baba Mosque, or Şeyh Nuri Efendi (Çarşamba) Lodge, is an Ottoman-era mosque in the Ahmediye quarter of Üsküdar, Istanbul. Built by Sheikh Kurban Nasuh Baba, it was begun in 1586 and opened in 1587.
en.Q6061848: Pervizoğlu Mosque is a historic mosque in the Yakutiye district of Erzurum.
en.Q6062531: Amcazade Hüseyin Pasha Mansion stands on the Bosphorus a little north of Anadoluhisarı. Built in 1699 for Grand Vizier Amcazade Hüseyin Pasha of the Köprülü family, it is the oldest surviving residence in Istanbul. Originally a much larger complex, only its main hall survives. Drafts of the Treaty of Karlowitz were prepared here.
en.Q6062970: Işıkkent is an area of Bornova, İzmir, covering the Egemenlik, Karacaoğlan and Işıklar neighbourhoods. İzmir's intercity bus terminal (İZOTAŞ) is here.
en.Q6064629: Çankırı Great Mosque, or Sultan Süleyman Mosque, dates from the era of Mimar Sinan. It was built by Sadık Kalfa on the orders of Suleiman the Magnificent.
en.Q6065399: Bet Yaakov Synagogue is on Heybeliada, one of Istanbul's islands. In the 1940s, when more than 250 Jewish families were spending their summers on the island, a synagogue was needed, and Bet Yaakov was built with official permission in 1953.
en.Q6065915: Şahidi Mosque is an Ottoman-era building in the Camikebir quarter of Muğla.
en.Q6066259: Gülbahar Hatun Mosque, also called Büyük İmaret or Hatuniye Mosque, was built in Trabzon in 1514 by Sultan Selim I in the name of his mother, Gülbahar Hatun.
en.Q6069700: Muğla Clock Tower, known locally as Saatli Kule, stands in the Balıbey quarter of Muğla, at the junction of Saatli Kule Street and Şeyh Camii Street, a central point of the old town. It is one of the finest works the Greeks who lived in Muğla left to the city.
en.Q6070960: The Kapuzbaşı Waterfalls are spring-fed waterfalls in the village of Kapuzbaşı, Yahyalı (Kayseri). One of them is said to be the highest waterfall in Türkiye. They are about 55 km from Yahyalı and from Aladağ (Adana), and 145 km from Kayseri.
en.Q6071250: The Dumlupınar War of Independence Martyrs' Memorial in the Dumlupınar district of Kütahya was built by the Ministry of Culture in memory of the Turkish soldiers who fell at the Battle of Dumlupınar. It opened on 30 August 1992, the 70th anniversary of the Great Offensive.
en.Q6073463: Beykoz Mecidiye Pavilion is a historic pavilion in the Beykoz district of Istanbul, south of the area called Hünkâr İskelesi in Yalıköy.
en.Q6074986: Haydarpaşa Pier is a historic pier building on the Asian side of Istanbul, designed by Vedat Tek.
en.Q6075000: Doğramacızade Ali Pasha Mosque is a mosque in the Bilkent area of Çankaya, Ankara.
en.Q6075775: Kastamonu Archaeology Museum displays archaeological finds collected from around Kastamonu and Çankırı.
en.Q6076389: Tekeli Mountain lies between the Doğanşar district of Sivas and the Almus district of Tokat.
en.Q607675: Parhali Monastery is a Georgian Orthodox monastery in the village of Altıparmak in the Yusufeli district of Artvin. Of the monastery complex built in the 9th–10th centuries, the main church and two chapels survive. In Turkish the name Parhali became Barhal.
en.Q6077054: Notre Dame de Lourdes is a Catholic church in the Göztepe quarter of İzmir.
en.Q6078142: The Uzbek Lodge (Özbekler Tekkesi) was founded in 1752 in Sultantepe, Üsküdar, by Naqshbandi dervishes from Bukhara in the tradition of Ahmed Yesevi. During the Turkish War of Independence it served as a secret base for sending soldiers and ammunition to Anatolia. It belongs to the General Directorate of Foundations, and there are plans to use it as a museum.
en.Q6078473: Lake Sera is a landslide-dammed lake in the Derecik valley between Yıldızlı and Derecik, in the Akçaabat district of Trabzon. It is named after Sera, the old name of Yıldızlı.
en.Q6079726: Merzifon Clock Tower stands in the centre of Merzifon, Amasya, above the monumental gate of the Çelebi Mehmet Madrasa.
en.Q6079823: Hacı Paşa Clock Tower is a clock tower in the Taşucu quarter of Silifke, Mersin.
en.Q6080071: The Great Victory Monument in Afyonkarahisar commemorates the city's liberation from Greek occupation and the Great Offensive. It was made by the sculptor Heinrich Krippel between 1934 and 1936 and opened by Prime Minister İsmet İnönü on 24 March 1936.
en.Q6080321: Cemil Topuzlu Pasha Mansion, also called İpar Mansion, is a three-storey Art Nouveau building in Çiftehavuzlar, Istanbul, built in the early 20th century.
en.Q6080493: The Antonine Fountain is a historic fountain in the ancient city of Sagalassos, in the Ağlasun district of Burdur.
en.Q6081037: Balıkesir Clock Tower stands on a slope inside the Municipal Park in Balıkesir.
en.Q6081542: The Atatürk House Museum is a two-storey historic building on Atatürk Avenue in Konya, built in 1912 of cut stone, rubble and brick. Registered to the Treasury in 1923, it served as the governor's residence and was reserved for Atatürk on his visits to Konya.
en.Q6082227: Aynalı Çarşı (also Halyo Çarşısı) is a covered bazaar in Çanakkale, built in 1890 by Eliyau Hallio, a leading member of the city's Jewish community. The door inscription has two texts, one in Ottoman Turkish and one in Ladino written in Hebrew letters.
en.Q6083081: Silahtar Ömer Pasha Mosque is in the town of Akça, Erbaa (Tokat). It was built of timber and cut stone using the çantı technique, without a single nail. It belongs to the General Directorate of Foundations and is still in use.
en.Q6083171: The Hannibal Monument was built in 1981 in memory of Hannibal on Hannibal Hill, within the TÜBİTAK grounds in Gebze.
en.Q6083245: Sumaki Höyük is a settlement mound on a limestone ridge west of Beşiri, Batman, overlooking a branch of the Yanarsu (formerly Garzan), a tributary of the Tigris. The mound measures 250 × 150 metres.
en.Q6083768: Kullar is an area of the Başiskele district of Kocaeli.
en.Q6084143: Çamkoru Nature Park lies in the Çamlıdere district, 110 km northwest of Ankara, and includes Çamkoru Pond. The old Ankara–Bolu highway cuts the 215-hectare park in two.
en.Q6085378: The Melik Gazi Tomb is in the Kayapaşa quarter of Niksar, Tokat. Melik Danişmend Gümüştekin Ahmet Gazi, founder of the Danishmendids, conquered Niksar and made it both a base against the coastal Byzantines and his capital.
en.Q6085562: The Tomb of Ertuğrul Gazi, father of Osman Gazi and a Seljuk frontier lord, is in the Söğüt district of Bilecik.
en.Q6085758: Ulaşlı is a neighbourhood in the Gölcük district of Kocaeli.
en.Q6086051: The Human Rights Monument is a monument in the Karşıyaka district of İzmir.
en.Q6086772: Sefaköy is a neighbourhood of Istanbul where many Balkan immigrants have settled.
en.Q6087240: İkitelli is an area in the west of Istanbul, within the Küçükçekmece and Başakşehir districts.
en.Q6089485: Mercimektepe Mound lies just east of Yozgat city, facing Çengeltepe Mound across the Yozgat–Sivas road. It measures 140 x 100 metres.
en.Q6089537: Merkez Efendi Mosque is a mosque at the Merkez Efendi Tomb in Zeytinburnu, Istanbul.
en.Q6089719: Kınık Höyük is a settlement mound southwest of Bilecik, about 5 km northwest of Pazaryeri as the crow flies, 300 metres from the main road at the Kınık village turn-off. It is 150 metres across and 4 metres high, with the Sorgun stream flowing past to the southeast.
en.Q6090543: Said Halim Pasha Mansion is a waterside mansion (yalı) in Yeniköy, Istanbul, also called the 'Lion Mansion' after the two lion statues on its quay. Built in neoclassical style in the last quarter of the 19th century, it has a calm exterior but rich arabesque decoration inside, recalling a small Arab palace.
en.Q6091056: Çengeltepe Mound lies 500 metres east of Yozgat city, south of the Sivas road, with Mercimektepe Mound rising just to its north. Both are thought to have been inhabited at the same time.
en.Q6091815: The Yörük Ali Efe Museum in the Yenipazar district of Aydın has been open since 2001. It was set up to keep alive the memory of the local hero Yörük Ali Efe, whose grave and statue stand in its garden.
en.Q6092334: Büyüktepe Höyük is a settlement mound 35 km southwest of Bayburt, 5 km north of Demirözü and 1 km north of Çiftetaş village, and is seen as the most important mound in the area. It is made of two hills joined by a saddle, in the well-watered Beşpınar Valley.
en.Q6093268: Pulur / Sakyol Höyük is a mound north-east of the village of Sakyol (formerly Pulur), now under the Keban Dam lake. It is recorded as Pulur / Sakyol to distinguish it from other mounds called Pulur in Anatolia.
en.Q6094187: Uludağ National Park covers 13,024 hectares south and southeast of Bursa and was declared a national park in 1961. It can be reached by road and by cable car. Many trails on the north and south slopes link its valleys and hills.
en.Q6095727: Kuriki Höyük is a mound made up of two hills about 70 metres apart, 14 km south of Batman and about 1 km southwest of Oymataş village, where the Batman river meets the Tigris.
en.Q6098573: Karahöyük 1 is a settlement mound about 7 km south-west of Konya city. Because there are several places called Karahöyük in Konya province, it is known as Karahöyük 1. It consists of eleven hillocks, one of them fairly large, and the settlement on them covers 1,000 x 500 metres.
en.Q6098580: Kemah Castle is in the Kemah district of Erzincan. It was built around 205 BC, probably by the Azrak kings. Held by the Safavids, it passed to the Ottoman Empire after the siege of Kemah in 1515. The castle covers 8,000 m² and rises 80 m; excavations were continuing as of 2019.
en.Q6098641: Mada Island, also called Kazak Island, is the largest of the 32 islands in Lake Beyşehir, at 822 hectares. The inhabited part, home to 180 people as of 2022, is called the Kumluca quarter and belongs to the village of Gedikli in Şarkikaraağaç, Isparta. The rest of the island lies within Kızıldağ National Park.
en.Q6098644: Yassıhöyük is a settlement mound 25 km north of Kırşehir, south of the village of Karahıdır. It measures 635 x 500 metres and is 12–13 metres high, about 30 km east of Kaman-Kalehöyük in the Kaman district.
en.Q6099232: İshaklı Han, also called Sâhib Ata Han, is a caravanserai on the old Afyon–Konya road in today's Sultandağı, formerly named İshaklı. It was built in 1249 by Sahip Ata Fahrettin Ali, during the reign of the Anatolian Seljuk sultan Kaykaus II.
en.Q6099398: Aktopraklık Mound is a settlement mound 25 km south-west of Bursa city centre, west of Nilüfer, on the eastern shore of Lake Uluabat. It is also known as Akçaları Sırtı Mound and Aktopraklık Mevkii.
en.Q6099419: The Atatürk and War of Independence Museum, officially the Anıtkabir Atatürk and War of Independence Museum, occupies a 3,000-square-metre colonnaded space below the Hall of Honour at Anıtkabir, where Atatürk's tomb lies. It opened to visitors on 21 June 1960.
en.Q6099582: Akmeşe is an area of İzmit, 30 km north-east of the city.
en.Q6099910: Girharrin Mound lies 11 km south-south-east of Mardin, just west of the Mardin–Nusaybin road, in the middle of Ortaköy village (formerly Girharrin); some sources call it Gülharrin. With its terraces it measures 400 x 300 metres and rises 40 metres.
en.Q6100053: Titriş Höyük lies 36 km north of Şanlıurfa as the crow flies and 18 km north-east of Karaköprü, partly beneath the village of Bahçeli. The mound itself covers 3.3 hectares, the settlement spreads over 33 hectares, and it rises 22 metres. It lies outside the Atatürk Dam reservoir.
en.Q6100614: Seyitömer Mound lies 24–25 km north-west of Kütahya as the crow flies, north-west of Seyitömer village, within the reserve land of the Seyitömer lignite mine. It measures 150 x 140 metres and is 24 metres high, with a flat area of about 2,000 m² on top.
en.Q6100677: Karagöl is a landslide-dammed lake 25–27 km from Borçka, Artvin. It lies within Borçka Karagöl Nature Park, set up on 14 August 2002. About 10,000 people visit the lake each year.
en.Q6100895: Eskiyapar Mound lies south of Çorum city, 6 km west of Alaca, on the Hüseyinabad Plain. In 1983–84 the village on top of it was moved so the mound could be protected and excavated. With a diameter of up to 350 metres and a height of 13 metres, it is one of the largest mounds in the region.
en.Q6101079: The Mater Dolorosa Catholic Church serves Samsun's Catholic community and belongs to the Roman Catholic Church. It is registered and protected as a first-degree historic site.
en.Q6101091: Çamdibi is an area of Bornova, İzmir, formerly a town, made up of seven neighbourhoods. Its residents are largely Balkan immigrants.
en.Q6101232: Keloğlan Cave is in the town of Dodurgalar in the Acıpayam district of Denizli, 3 km from the Denizli–Antalya highway. The cave is 5–6 metres high on average, with a 145-metre visitor route.
en.Q6101388: Küllüoba Mound lies 35 km south-east of Eskişehir city, 15 km north-east of Seyitgazi and 1,300 m south of the village of Yenikent. It measures 300 x 150 metres and is 10 metres high, north of the Phrygian highlands and west of the upper Sakarya plains.
en.Q6101802: Türbe Höyük is a mound 27 km south-west of Siirt, on a stream bank in the Botan valley about 6 km north of where the Botan joins the Tigris. It measures about 100 x 40 metres.
en.Q6103054: Hasandede is a village in the central district of Kırıkkale.
en.Q6103257: Lala Mustafa Pasha Mosque in the central Yakutiye district was built by Lala Mustafa Pasha and is the first Ottoman mosque in Erzurum.
en.Q6103642: Uğurlu / Zeytinli is a settlement mound on the western side of Gökçeada (Çanakkale), 900 m east-north-east of Uğurlu village, about 1,400 m from Uğurlu harbour and 23–24 km from the island's centre. The settlement lies on the eastern slope of İsa Tepe (Doğanlı Tepe).
en.Q6103865: Alikahya is an area of İzmit, Kocaeli.
en.Q61071758: Akgöl is a freshwater alluvial-dam lake between the Karasu and Ferizli districts of Sakarya, formed by sediment from the Sakarya river, which flows about 1 km away.
en.Q61072477: Cizre Great Mosque is a historic mosque in the Dağkapı quarter of central Cizre, Şırnak.
en.Q61072484: Adıyaman Grand Mosque is in the centre of Adıyaman. Its first construction date is unknown, but it is thought to have been built between 1506 and 1515 by the Dulkadirid ruler Durak Bey. The mosque took its present form in 1863.
en.Q61072504: Antakya Great Mosque was a mosque in the Antakya district of Hatay. Showing Seljuk architectural features, it was built by the Mamluks between 1268 and 1271 and thoroughly repaired in the early 18th century (AH 1117). It was considered the oldest and largest mosque in Hatay and was completely destroyed in the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake.
en.Q61072508: Edincik Grand Mosque is in the town of Edincik in the Bandırma district of Balıkesir. According to its inscription it was built in 1382 (784 AH) by İldutan Bin Abdullah. In 1888 Nuri Usta of Edincik extended the prayer hall walls, giving the mosque its present look; the ablution fountain was added in 1900.
en.Q61072520: Hasankeyf Grand Mosque is a mosque in Hasankeyf, Batman. Its first construction date is unknown, but its architecture places it among the mosques of the Artuqid period (1101–1232).
en.Q61072521: Bayburt Grand Mosque is a Friday mosque in Bayburt. It is believed to date from the reign of the Anatolian Seljuk sultan Mesud II (1282–1298) and was rebuilt in the 1970s true to its original plan.
en.Q61072524: Bitlis Grand Mosque is in the centre of Bitlis. According to its inscription it was built in 1153 by Ebul Muzaffer Muhammed of the Marwanids, vassals of the Seljuk sultan Tughril Bey. Badly damaged during the Russian occupation, it underwent major repairs in 1985.
en.Q61072532: Burdur Grand Mosque is a mosque in the Pazar quarter of Burdur. It was first built in 1300 by Dündar Bey of the Hamidids and restored in 1749 by Çelik Mehmet Pasha. Damaged by earthquakes, it was rebuilt with a timber frame in 1919.
en.Q61072563: Çorum Great Mosque, also called the Murad IV Great Mosque, Sultan Alaeddin Mosque or Cami-i Kebir, is believed to have been built in the late 13th century by Hayreddin Bey, a freed slave of the Seljuk sultan Alaeddin Keykubad III. It is rich in woodwork and has no inscription.
en.Q61072567: Sungurlu Great Mosque in the Sungurlu district of Çorum was built by Mehmet Sungur Bey in 1762 and repaired by the General Directorate of Foundations in 1984, 1994 and 2015. It has a square, domed plan, with a three-bay porch on the north side covered by three domes.
en.Q61072933: Çelebi Mehmet Madrasa Mosque, also known as Medreseönü Mosque or Murad II Mosque, was built in Merzifon in 1427 next to the Çelebi Mehmet Madrasa, on the order of Murad II, the sixth Ottoman sultan.
en.Q61073765: Yeşilli Mosque is a historic mosque in the Eski Kuyumcular quarter of Balıkesir.
en.Q61073769: The Sümerbank Headquarters Building stands on Ali Hikmet Paşa Square, where Zağnos Paşa Street meets Milli Kuvvetler Street in Balıkesir, and is one of the city's symbols.
en.Q61074659: The Martyr Standard-Bearer Mehmetçik Monument stands near Zafertepeçalköy in the Altıntaş district of Kütahya and is dedicated to those who fell in the Turkish War of Independence.
en.Q61075536: Kaleiçi is a district of Merkezefendi, Denizli, once enclosed by land walls and now used as a market area. It was the first settlement of Denizli under the Anatolian Seljuks, with an inner and an outer castle wall; the outer walls have vanished, while traces of the inner walls survive in places.
en.Q61075807: Şahinkaya Canyon is in the Vezirköprü district of Samsun and forms the deepest part of the Altınkaya Dam lake. Türkiye's second-largest canyon after Ulubey Canyon, it is about 1,500 metres long and 324 metres deep. It was declared a national tourism area in 2012 and a nature park in 2015.
en.Q61075941: Ölüdeniz-Kıdrak Nature Park is a nature park in the Fethiye district of Muğla.
en.Q61076080: Pazar Mosque is a historic mosque in the İlkadım district of Samsun, an Ilkhanid-period building dated 1380. The rectangular, single-storey mosque has rubble stone walls and a wooden roof. It was repaired in 1819 and in the early Republican years and has partly lost its original character.
en.Q61076081: Pazar Mosque is a historic single-storey timber mosque in the Terme district of Samsun, from the first half of the 19th century, with a tiled roof. Its minaret, demolished in 1939, was replaced in 1961. Restoration began in 2017, and it reopened for worship on 29 May 2020.
en.Q61076266: Portakal Çiçeği Park is a park in the Çankaya district of Ankara, named after the Portakal Çiçeği Valley where it lies and the Portakal Çiçeği Tower in the valley. Of its 44,700 square metres, 40,000 are landscaped, 100 are a pool and 100 a sports ground.
en.Q61076441: Rize Museum, also called Rize Ethnography Museum, Tuzcuoğlu Mansion or the Yellow House, is in the Piriçelebi quarter of central Rize. It has occupied this 19th-century house, a fine example of local civil architecture, since 27 June 1998.
en.Q61076446: Fevkani Church, or Nizip Fevkani Church, stands in the Fevkani quarter of Nizip. It is thought to date from the 12th century and was converted into a mosque in the 1800s. It fell out of use after the Şıhlar Mosque (1888) and Molla Ahmet Mosque (1904) opened.
en.Q61076450: Mikron Bridge is a 19th-century arch bridge over the Fırtına stream, 2 km from Çamlıhemşin, Rize. It is 41 metres long, 3.1 metres wide and 11 metres high; its piers were set wide apart against floods.
en.Q61076451: Timisvat Bridge, or Köprüköy Bridge (later renamed Osmanlı Köprüsü), is an 18th-century arch bridge over the Fırtına stream, 10 km from Ardeşen, Rize. It is 35 metres long, 2.7 metres wide and 13 metres high.
en.Q61076454: Şenyuva Bridge is a single-arch bridge over the Fırtına stream, 7 km from Çamlıhemşin, Rize. Built in 1696, it is 40 metres long and 20 metres high, with a pointed arch. Its inscription was lost in the 1946 flood.
en.Q61076466: Dereköy Bridge is a single-arch bridge with a flattened pointed arch in the İkizdere district of Rize. Its arch and parapets are of cut stone and the rest of rubble stone, with a deck of neat rubble. The parapets are square at the base and oval on top, and there are small niches inside the arch abutments, which rest on bedrock.
en.Q61076470: Bulut Waterfall in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize is the highest waterfall in Türkiye, dropping about 250 metres in four steps. It is fed by the Tar stream, which rises on the Altıparmak range of the Kaçkar Mountains; Seyran Tepe, where it lies, is at 2,451 metres.
en.Q61076472: Palovit Waterfall is in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize, inside Kaçkar Mountains National Park. Fed by the Palovit stream, it falls 15 metres and is one of the highest-flow waterfalls in Rize.
en.Q61076474: Gelintülü Waterfall is in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize. Fed by the Kavron stream, it falls 15 metres at an altitude of 1,320 metres.
en.Q61076476: Ağaran Waterfall is in the Çayeli district of Rize, 12 km from Çayeli. Fed by the Şairler stream, it takes its name ('whitening') from the white foam it throws off as it falls from a high, steep rock.
en.Q61076505: Ciha Castle is a castle in the Pazar district of Rize, 7 km from Pazar and east of the Hemşin stream. Thought to have been built by the Genoese in the 14th century for signalling and watch, it has a circular plan and an entrance flanked by two towers on the north-east.
en.Q61076536: Ciha Castle is a castle on Ciha Hill, which separates the Arhavi and Hopa districts of Artvin.
en.Q61076619: Güzeldere Waterfall Nature Park covers 22.76 hectares in the village of Güzeldere, Gölyaka (Düzce). It was declared a nature park in 2011.
en.Q61076675: The Rize Atatürk Statue is in the Piriçelebi quarter of Rize. It made the news when it was removed from the 15 July Democracy and Republic Square where it stood.
en.Q61076964: Zindan Cave is in the Aksu district of Isparta, about 2 km north-east of Aksu town.
en.Q61077823: Karaahmetli Nature Park covers 107 hectares in the village of Karaahmetli, Bahşılı (Kırıkkale). It was declared a nature park by a cabinet decision of 23 July 2009.
en.Q63349559: Sülüklü Han, or Kazancılar Hanı, is a historic inn in the Sur district of Diyarbakır. It was built of black basalt in 1683 by Hanilioğlu Mahmut Çelebi and his sister Atike Hatun. Its name comes from the leeches taken from the well in its courtyard for medical use.
en.Q63372405: Nebi Mosque, also known as the Prophet's Mosque, is a historic mosque in the Sur district of Diyarbakır, built in the 15th century under the Aq Qoyunlu.
en.Q63372490: Gazi Pavilion, or Atatürk Pavilion, is a two-storey historic mansion in Diyarbakır from the 15th century, known as an Aq Qoyunlu work and formerly called Semanoğlu Pavilion. During the First World War, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, commander of the 16th Corps, used it as his headquarters from 14 March 1916 to 27 March 1917.
en.Q64214968: Klarjeti Castle is an old castle in the village of Klarjeti (now Bereket) in the Ardanuç district of Artvin, in southwestern historic Georgia. It stands on a rock 700 m west of the village centre, 1,440 m above sea level. The 32 × 30 m castle has two towers and is thought to have played an important role in the medieval Klarjeti region, which is named after it.
en.Q64699469: Ephesus is a World Heritage Site in the Selçuk district of İzmir. It was added to the tentative list in 1994; Türkiye's 2001 application for full listing was deferred by the World Heritage Committee, and the site was inscribed in 2015.
en.Q6481645: Çayırbağı is a neighbourhood in the Düzköy district of Trabzon.
en.Q6495441: Çalköy is a neighbourhood in the Düzköy district of Trabzon, home to Çal Cave.
en.Q65219967: Bursa Muradiye Mosque was built in Bursa in the first half of the 15th century by the Ottoman sultan Murad II.
en.Q65220056: The Nation Monument (Ulus Anıtı) in Eskişehir stands at the Station Junction on İsmet İnönü Street.
en.Q65220312: Gölcük Lake is an artificial lake 13 km south of Bolu. It covers 4.5 hectares, has a 1,300 m shoreline and lies at 1,217 m. The lake and its surroundings are protected as a nature park. The building on the shore is a state guesthouse of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry.
en.Q65220334: Mardin Great Mosque is a historic Artuqid mosque in central Mardin, built of cut stone and originally with two minarets. Its dome is ribbed on the outside, a style that later became a tradition in Mardin architecture. The mosque is wider than it is deep, with a dome in front of the mihrab and a rectangular courtyard to the north.
en.Q65220544: Seka Park in İzmit was created on the site of the former Seka paper mill. It lies in the city centre on the shore of the Gulf of İzmit, beside the D-100 highway.
en.Q65284740: Engüzek Castle is a medieval Georgian castle in the historical Tao region, in the village of Dikyar in the Uzundere district of Erzurum. It is named after the village's old name, Üngüzek or Engüzek; medieval sources call it Ağca Kala. It is also known as Engüzekkapı Castle.
en.Q65285170: Peterek (Perktekrek) Castle is a historic castle in the Yusufeli district of Artvin.
en.Q65285973: Mere Church is a medieval Georgian church in the village of Çakırkoç, formerly Mere, in the Posof district of Ardahan, in the Turkish part of the historic Samtskhe region. Being near Mere Castle, it is also known as Mere Castle Church.
en.Q65286988: Sveti Church is a medieval Georgian church in the Gündoğdu quarter of Seyitler village in the central district of Artvin, in the historic Klarjeti region. It is also known as Kilise Kapısı Church after the quarter's old name.
en.Q65293171: Çala Church is a medieval Georgian church in the village of Doğruyol (formerly Çala) in the Arpaçay district of Kars. Standing in the village centre and dedicated to the Virgin Mary, it is one of the finest buildings of the Tao-Klarjeti region for its carved stone decoration.
en.Q6540627: Yalı is a neighbourhood in the Bodrum district of Muğla.
en.Q6581129: Pierre Loti Hill is a hill overlooking the Golden Horn in the Eyüpsultan district of Istanbul. It is named after the French novelist and orientalist Julien Viaud (Pierre Loti), who came to Istanbul in 1876 and often visited a coffee house on the hill.
en.Q6608996: Korsanlar Cave (Pirates' Cave) is a cave in the Alanya district of Antalya.
en.Q6618993: Kesikköprü is a village in the central district of Kırşehir.
en.Q66371383: Sivas Archaeology Museum occupies a building put up in 1914 by Governor Ahmed Muammer Bey as a vocational school workshop. It has been a museum since 1983.
en.Q66475469: Kemeraltı Mosque is a place of worship in the Seyhan district of Adana. It is also known as Savcıoğlu or Savcızade Mosque after its founder, and as Tarsuskapı Mosque after its location.
en.Q6872777: Bahçecik is an area of the Başiskele district of Kocaeli, south of the Gulf of İzmit at the foot of the Samanlı Mountains. Until the early 20th century its population was mostly Armenian.
en.Q6903317: The Monastery of St George (Aya Yorgi) is a monastery on Büyükada.
en.Q6921470: Altındere is a neighbourhood of Akyazı, Sakarya, at the foot of Mount Keremali.
en.Q6940214: Surp Sarkis Armenian Orthodox Church is a historic church in the Sur district of Diyarbakır, also known as the Hızır İlyas Church or Çeltik Church. It belongs to the Orthodox Armenian community.
en.Q6970952: Cizre Castle is a ruined castle on the bank of the Tigris in Cizre, Şırnak, with inner and outer parts. Two-thirds of its walls have vanished, and some stones of the surviving southern section were taken for house building.
en.Q769148: Dim Cave is a show cave near Alanya, Antalya.
en.Q794826: Âşıklar Cave (Lovers' Cave) is a cave in the Alanya district of Antalya.
en.Q803676: Bahçeşehir is an area of Istanbul in the Başakşehir and Esenyurt districts, north-west of Lake Küçükçekmece, that has grown as a planned satellite town.
en.Q836958: Göltürkbükü is a neighbourhood in the Bodrum district of Muğla.
en.Q85694471: Deliller Hanı, or Hüsrev Pasha Hanı, is a historic inn in the Sur district of Diyarbakır. A foundation deed of 1603 calls it the Mardin Gate Staging Inn. Today it is run as a hotel and known as the Kervansaray Hotel.
en.Q85961663: Cemil Pasha Mansion is a historic mansion in the Sur district of Diyarbakır. After restoration it is now used as the Diyarbakır City Museum.
en.Q85968057: Apivanak Bridge is an arch bridge over the Palovit stream, a tributary of the Fırtına, in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize. It is 15 metres long, 2.5 metres wide and 2 metres above the ground, on old trade routes.
en.Q85968999: The Church of St Nicholas in Bodrum was a Greek Orthodox church built in 1780 or 1873 and dedicated to St Nicholas. After the Greek–Turkish population exchange it was used as a sponge store, a cinema and an adult education centre, and in 1969 it was demolished in a controlled way after being declared unsafe. Its remains are on Hilmi Uran Square on Cumhuriyet Street.
en.Q85969061: Bozburun Lighthouse is a lighthouse in the Armutlu district of Yalova.
en.Q85972072: Kemal Sonunur Park is a city park in the Eryaman area of Etimesgut, Ankara.
en.Q85975617: Tunca Bridge is a stone-paved arch bridge in the town of Tunca, 22 km from Ardeşen, Rize. It crosses the Tunca stream and is 28 metres long, 2.8 metres wide and 11 metres high; it is reached by a stone-stepped path south of the village.
en.Q86093389: The Temple of Mithras stands inside Zerzevan Castle in the Çınar district of Diyarbakır.
en.Q86669830: Çifte Han, or Borsa Hanı, is a historic inn in the Sur district of Diyarbakır, an Ottoman work believed to date from the 16th century. It was planned as a pair of inns, but the second was demolished when a road was opened. Both were built of cut basalt. Once used as an exchange, it is now in ruins.
en.Q86835189: The Hamiye Çolakoğlu Ceramics Museum is a ceramics and biography museum in Ankara. Founded within Hacettepe University's Faculty of Fine Arts, it is in the Ankara State Conservatory building on the Beytepe Campus.
en.Q87069499: İskender Pasha Mosque is in the Sur district of Diyarbakır. Construction began in 1551 or 1554 on the orders of Çerkes İskender Pasha, the 12th Ottoman governor of the Diyarbekir province, and was finished in 1557. Some sources name Mimar Sinan as its architect, but this is not certain.
en.Q87265638: Melek Ahmed Pasha Mosque is a historic mosque in the Sur district of Diyarbakır, built in the 16th century by Melek Ahmed Pasha. Its plan and architecture show the influence of Mimar Sinan.
en.Q87270204: Hadım Ali Pasha Mosque (Mizgefta Elî Pasha) is a historic mosque in the quarter of the same name in Sur, Diyarbakır.
en.Q87272209: Hüsrev Pasha Mosque is a historic mosque in the quarter of the same name in Sur, Diyarbakır, built by Divane Hüsrev Pasha. Evliya Çelebi, who visited Diyarbakır in 1655, described it as a 'charming' mosque near the Mardin Gate with a large congregation.
en.Q87407787: The Inner Citadel (İç Kale) is considered the first settlement of Diyarbakır. It lies in the north-east of the city, about 100 m above the Tigris river.
en.Q87443642: Nasuh Pasha Mosque is a historic mosque in the Sur district of Diyarbakır.
en.Q87719527: Latifiye Madrasa is a historic madrasa in the Sur district of Diyarbakır.
en.Q87738382: Mesudiye Madrasa is a historic madrasa in the Sur district of Diyarbakır.
en.Q87738983: Zinciriye Madrasa, also known as Sincariye Madrasa, is a historic madrasa in the Sur district of Diyarbakır.
en.Q87761549: Deva Bath is a historic hamam in the Sur district of Diyarbakır. It is also called Deve (Camel) Bath, after an old story of a camel that went missing from a caravan and was found here after several days of searching.
en.Q87767582: Melek Ahmed Pasha Bath is a historic hamam near the city gates in Sur, Diyarbakır, built as part of a mosque complex. Only its changing hall survives.
en.Q87768122: Paşa Bath, also known as Behram Pasha Bath, is a historic hamam in the Sur district of Diyarbakır.
en.Q87768671: Vahap Ağa Bath is a historic hamam in the Sur district of Diyarbakır.
en.Q88273428: Palu Castle is a historic castle built on rock in the Palu district of Elazığ. It dates from the Urartian period and was built by the Urartian king Menua. The Murat river surrounds it on the south and south-east, and steep slopes on the north and west made it naturally defensible and hard to capture.
en.Q88653543: Ömer Şeddat Mosque, popularly called Hz. Ömer Mosque, is a historic mosque in the Sur district of Diyarbakır, built against the city walls west of the Mardin Gate.
en.Q896117: Bozdağ is a 2,421-metre mountain in Denizli province, between the Acıpayam–Gireniz valley and the Barza plain of Tavas. It is one of the peaks of the Gölgeli Mountains and has few passes.
en.Q89718384: The Sebasteion Temple is within the Carian settlement near Geyre village in the Karacasu district of Aydın.
en.Q90004343: Kadı Mosque is a mosque from the Aq Qoyunlu period in the Sur district of Diyarbakır.
en.Q90563022: Derman Fountain is a fountain made by the Turkish ceramic artist and academic Hamiye Çolakoğlu. It is an important example of contemporary ceramic art shown in public spaces.
en.Q93392457: Niğde Castle is a historic castle on the hill of old Niğde.
en.Q9357515: The Alanya Shipyard and Alanya Arsenal are historic buildings in Alanya from the Seljuk period.
en.Q959497: Körtik Tepe, also written Körtiktepe, is a settlement mound right next to Ağıl village in the Bismil district of Diyarbakır. Before its discovery the site was farmland.
en.Q96023275: Limni Lake is in the village of Zigana in the Torul district of Gümüşhane, surrounded by spruce, Scots pine, juniper, fir, blackberry and purple- and yellow-flowered rhododendron. Sources give its altitude as anything from 1,700 to 2,100 metres.
en.Q96651579: Miletus Museum is an archaeology museum within the ancient city of Miletus, near Balat village in the Didim district of Aydın.
en.Q96738974: The Atatürk and Youth Monument stands at the very centre of Hacettepe University's Beytepe Campus. It was made in 1991 by the artist Remzi Savaş, a lecturer at the university's Faculty of Fine Arts. It consists of a sculpture group led by a figure of Atatürk, with three interlocking arches rising behind.
en.Q97205392: Kov Castle is a castle 22 km south-east of central Gümüşhane.
en.Q97205834: The Orhan Gazi Complex is a group of buildings in Bursa commissioned by the Ottoman sultan Orhan Gazi in the 14th century.
en.Q97206355: Torul Castle, also called Toğrul or Ardasa Castle, is east of Torul, Gümüşhane. Now in ruins, it was built as a fire tower for signalling. Its gate is on the east side, and it stands about 200 metres high; its walls are of rubble and dressed stone in the colour of the natural rock.
en.Q97207430: Canca Castle, or Tzaniha Castle, is built on rocky ground west of Gümüşhane, at an altitude of 1,530 metres. A restoration contract worth 1.8 million lira was tendered in 2018. The partly rounded castle is built of rubble stone.
en.Q97207580: Demirciler Bridge is the last bridge, counting downstream, on the Çhala stream, a tributary of the Çoruh, in the Borçka district of Artvin. It is also called Makreti Bridge, as it was built within the old village of Makreti, now named Kale.
en.Q97209322: Çal Cave is in the Düzköy district of Trabzon. Its development was completed in 2000 and it opened to tourism in 2003. Sources put it at 1,050 or 1,116 metres above sea level. A castle stands above the cave, and in wet seasons a stream runs through it.
en.Q97220855: Damlataş (Sincan) Cave is a karst cave near the village of Sincan in the Payas district of Hatay, on the slopes of the Nur Mountains at 542 m. It is 95 m long, formed in Jurassic–Cretaceous dolomite and dolomitic limestone, and is a fossil cave that has stopped developing.
en.Q97222381: Pertek Sungur Bey Mosque, also called Baysungur Mosque or the Upper Mosque, was built by Sungur Bey in the second half of the 16th century in the Pertek district of Tunceli.
en.Q97233362: Alacadağ is a faulted mountain on the Teke Peninsula in Antalya Province, on the Demre–Finike border. It runs southwest to northeast and is 2,328 m high. It looks like the seaward end of the Bey Mountains but is separated from them by the Akçay river. It is 30 km long north to south and 20 km wide east to west.
en.Q97233373: Alacadağ is a volcanic mountain in south-west Konya province, mostly within the Seydişehir district.
en.Q97237800: Kızıltepe Great Mosque, also called Dunaysır or Koçhisar Great Mosque, is in Kızıltepe, Mardin. It was begun by the Mardin Artuqid ruler Yavlak Arslan (1184–1200) and, after his death, completed by his brother Artuk Arslan in 1204–1205.
en.Q97316427: Tortum Castle is a medieval Georgian castle in the historical Tao region, in the village of Tortumkale (formerly Tortum) in the Tortum district of Erzurum.
en.Q97320238: Sudüşen Waterfall is on the Nacaklı stream, 8 km from the Üvezpınar quarter in Yalova, at an altitude of about 250 metres. Tours run from Yalova (43 km); a 120-metre panorama hill overlooks the falls, and the pool below is suitable for swimming.
en.Q97320455: Hapsiyaş Bridge (Kiremitli Köprü) is a historic bridge in the Bölümlü quarter of Of, Trabzon, built around 1935 by Abdülaziz Sandıkçı. A Republican-era bridge, it carried people, vehicles and animals in its day.
en.Q97321105: Kaz Gölü is a tectonic lake in Tokat province near the town of Üzümören on the Zile–Pazar road, on the Kazova plain in Turhal close to the Pazar district border.
en.Q97368741: Halid Ağa Fountain is a fountain in the Kadıköy district of Istanbul, built in 1794 or 1795 by Halid Ağa, Chief Eunuch of the palace, and repaired in 1838/39 and 1868/69.
en.Q97387317: Tohumoğlu Bridge crosses the Harşit stream 17 km east of Gümüşhane. It is about 65 metres long and 5.35 metres wide. Together with the Gümüşhane Bridge, it was built in October 1575 by Ferruh Zad Oğlu Halebi. It has two round arches and a flood opening in its pier; the rubble-paved deck slopes.
en.Q97387392: Imera Monastery, or the Monastery of St John Prodromos, is in the village of Olucak, Gümüşhane. According to written sources it was built in 1350 and renovated in 1859 by the nun Roxane.
en.Q97648638: Ahmed Afif Pasha Mansion, also called Muhayyeş Mansion or Kemal Uzan Mansion, is a waterside mansion on the European shore of the Bosphorus between İstinye and Yeniköy, probably built between 1900 and 1910.
en.Q97924802: Ereğli Great Mosque in the Ereğli district of Konya was built in 1426 by Mehmet Bey, son of the Karamanid İbrahim Bey. Its minaret, one of the oldest in Türkiye, was built in 1116 as a watchtower under the Seljuk sultan Mesud I.
en.Q97924808: Doğanhisar Great Mosque is in the Doğanhisar district of Konya. According to the inscription above its door, it was built in 1548.
en.Q97924889: Kilis Great Mosque, in the Hacı Gümüş quarter, is the oldest and largest mosque in Kilis. Despite Ottoman-era repairs it keeps its original architecture. Its first construction date is unknown; it was rebuilt in 1388 by Hacı Halil son of Abdullah and repaired in 1912 and 1924.
en.Q97947254: Kayseri Great Mosque, also known as Sultan Mosque or Cami-i Kebir, is in the centre of Kayseri and was built around the mid-12th century.
en.Q97947293: Hızır Bey Mosque, popularly called the Great Mosque, is in the Eğirdir district of Isparta. Its original date is unknown, but it may have been built by Hızır Bey in the first quarter of the 14th century. It burned in a fire in 1814 and was rebuilt in its original form.
en.Q97947295: Kars Great Mosque is in the Kaleiçi quarter of Kars. It was built in 1643 by Dilaver Pasha, governor of Kars under Sultan Ibrahim. It was burned during the Russian occupation of Kars after the 1877–1878 Russo-Ottoman War, damaged in the First World War and further ruined by earthquakes after the war.
en.Q97947297: Kastamonu Great Mosque, also called Atabeygazi Mosque or the Forty-Column Mosque after the 40 columns inside, was built in 1273 by Atabey Muzaffereddin Yavlak Aslan Bey. A tomb thought to be its founder's stands next to it.
en.Q97947300: Kutlu Bey Mosque, also known as Isparta Great Mosque, is a mosque in Isparta. It was rebuilt on the orders of Abdulhamid II in 1899, on the foundations of a mosque known to exist in 1429, and completed in 1904. That building collapsed in an earthquake in 1914; the present mosque dates from 1922.
en.Q97947314: Tire Great Mosque is a mosque in the Tire district of İzmir. A repair inscription of 1870 above its north door records that it was built by Cüneyd Bey of the Aydınids.
en.Q97947316: Tokat Great Mosque is a mosque in Tokat.
en.Q97947323: Van Great Mosque stands within the old city of Van. The building is largely ruined and its inscription has not been found. Oktay Aslanapa excavated it between 1970 and 1973.
en.Q98091568: Birecik Great Mosque is in the Birecik district of Şanlıurfa. Some researchers date it to the 12th century, but its damaged inscription shows it was built in 1365 by the Mamluk sultan al-Ashraf Shaban.
en.Q98091570: Bor Great Mosque, or Sultan Alaaddin Mosque, in the Bor district of Niğde is the oldest building in Bor and has partly kept its original architecture. According to its inscription it was built by Hacı Hoca in 1410–1411, in the reign of the Karamanid sultan Nasireddin Mehmed II, and named after his father Alaeddin I.
en.Q98091585: Halfeti Great Mosque in the Halfeti district of Şanlıurfa was built between 1804 and 1807. When the Birecik Dam began filling in 2001, the lower part of the mosque was flooded.
en.Q98091586: Harran Great Mosque, also called the Great Mosque or the Paradise Mosque, is in the Harran district of Şanlıurfa. The oldest mosque of Islamic architecture in Türkiye, it was built between 744 and 750 by the Umayyad caliph Marwan II.
en.Q98091589: Karamanoğlu Mosque, also called Karamanoğlu İbrahim Bey Mosque, İbrahim Bey Mosque or Ürgüp Great Mosque, is in the Ürgüp district of Nevşehir. It was built in the 13th century by Vizier İbrahim Bey of the Karamanid state.
en.Q98091600: Midyat Great Mosque, also known as Cevatpaşa Mosque after its founder, is in the Midyat district of Mardin. It was built by Cevat Pasha in 1925.
en.Q98091601: Milas Great Mosque, also known as Ahmed Gazi Mosque, is in the Milas district of Muğla. According to its inscription it was built in 1364 by Emir Ahmed Gazi Bey. It has been repaired several times since 1879; in a three-month project from May to August 2022 its roof and minaret timbers were replaced and the lead of its dome and minaret renewed.
en.Q98091603: Muş Great Mosque stands west of the Alaeddin Bey and Hacı Şeref mosques in Muş and has no inscription. It is thought to have first been built in 979 by Sheikh Muhammed-i Mağribi; its architecture shows a newer building on top of an older one. It was an Armenian church converted into a mosque.
en.Q98091621: Siirt Great Mosque is a mosque in Siirt. Its original date is unknown; after falling into ruin it was repaired in 1129 by the Iraqi Seljuk ruler Mughith al-Din Mahmud and in 1260 by the atabeg Mücahid İshak.
en.Q98091629: Tavşanlı Great Mosque is in the Tavşanlı district of Kütahya. The first mosque, of unknown date, is thought to have been built by Arslan Bey in the Germiyanid period; the present mosque was built on its foundations in the 19th century under Abdulhamid II.
en.Q98091641: Şarkışla Great Mosque in the Şarkışla district of Sivas was built in 1669 by Üsküdarlı Mehmet Ağa.
en.Q981506: Kurşunlu Waterfall is reached by turning left at km 24 of the Antalya–Isparta road and driving 7 km.
en.Q98690921: Çankırı Museum is a museum in the province of Çankırı, Türkiye.
en.Q98743303: 15 July Democracy Martyrs Square is on the shore of the Gulf of İzmir in the Mithatpaşa quarter of Konak. It was created by putting the stretch of Mustafa Kemal Coastal Boulevard in front of Mithatpaşa Park underground, and opened on 17 February 2019.
en.Q991449: Esztergom Castle, officially the Esztergom Turkish Culture Centre, is a cultural centre in the Keçiören district of Ankara. It opened on 29 May 2005 and is a replica of Esztergom Castle in Hungary.
